#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Review a Dockerfile for security, image size, build cache, and reliability problems.

Usage:
  python3 lint_dockerfile.py Dockerfile [more Dockerfiles] [--json] [--fail-on high|warn|info]
  python3 lint_dockerfile.py - < Dockerfile

Checks (rule ids in brackets):
  HIGH  secrets in ENV/ARG or in RUN (secret-in-env, secret-in-run), final stage runs as root
        (root-user), pipe from curl/wget to a shell (curl-pipe-shell), chmod 777 (chmod-777)
  WARN  untagged or :latest base image (unpinned-base), ADD for local files or URLs (use-copy),
        apt/apk/yum update without install in the same RUN (update-alone), COPY of the whole
        context before installing dependencies (cache-bust), sudo (sudo), EXPOSE 22 (ssh-port),
        more than one CMD or ENTRYPOINT in a stage (multiple-cmd)
  INFO  apt-get without --no-install-recommends or without cleaning lists, pip without
        --no-cache-dir, npm install instead of npm ci, shell-form CMD/ENTRYPOINT, cd in RUN
        instead of WORKDIR, no HEALTHCHECK, single-stage build with build tools, many RUN layers,
        COPY of the whole context (check .dockerignore)
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 findings at or above --fail-on (default high), 2 usage or read error.
Python 3 standard library only.
"""
import json
import re
import shlex
import sys

LEVELS = {"info": 0, "warn": 1, "high": 2}
SECRET_KEY = re.compile(r"(PASSWORD|PASSWD|SECRET|TOKEN|API_?KEY|ACCESS_?KEY|PRIVATE_?KEY|CREDENTIALS?)", re.I)
BUILD_TOOLS = re.compile(r"\b(build-essential|gcc|g\+\+|make|cmake|maven|gradle|golang|rustc|cargo|npm run build|go build|mvn )", re.I)


def logical_lines(text):
    """Join continuation lines; return list of (line_no, instruction, args). Skips comments and parser directives."""
    out, buf, start = [], "", None
    escape = "\\"
    for i, raw in enumerate(text.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n"), 1):
        m = re.match(r"^#\s*escape\s*=\s*(\S)", raw)
        if m and not out and not buf:
            escape = m.group(1)
            continue
        s = raw.strip()
        if not buf and (not s or s.startswith("#")):
            continue
        if buf and s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if start is None:
            start = i
        if s.endswith(escape):
            buf += s[:-1] + " "
            continue
        buf += s
        parts = buf.split(None, 1)
        out.append((start, parts[0].upper(), parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""))
        buf, start = "", None
    if buf:
        parts = buf.split(None, 1)
        out.append((start, parts[0].upper(), parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""))
    return out


def review(text):
    lines = logical_lines(text)
    findings = []

    def add(level, rule, line, msg, fix):
        findings.append({"level": level, "rule": rule, "line": line, "message": msg, "fix": fix})

    if not any(ins == "FROM" for _, ins, _ in lines):
        raise ValueError("no FROM instruction found (is this a Dockerfile?)")
    stages, cur = [], None
    for ln, ins, args in lines:
        if ins == "FROM":
            m = re.match(r"(?:--platform=\S+\s+)?(\S+)(?:\s+AS\s+(\S+))?", args, re.I)
            cur = {"line": ln, "image": m.group(1) if m else args, "name": m.group(2) if m else None, "ins": []}
            stages.append(cur)
        elif cur is not None:
            cur["ins"].append((ln, ins, args))
    names = {s["name"].lower() for s in stages if s["name"]}
    arg_names = {a.split("=")[0].strip() for _, i, a in lines if i == "ARG"}

    for s in stages:
        img = s["image"]
        if img.lower() in names or img == "scratch" or img.startswith("$"):
            pass
        elif "@sha256:" in img:
            pass
        elif ":" not in img.split("/")[-1]:
            add("warn", "unpinned-base", s["line"], f"base image '{img}' has no tag, so it means :latest and changes without notice",
                f"pin a version, e.g. {img}:<version>-slim, or a digest")
        elif img.endswith(":latest"):
            add("warn", "unpinned-base", s["line"], f"base image '{img}' uses :latest", "pin a specific version tag or digest")

    final = stages[-1]
    run_count = 0
    for idx, s in enumerate(stages):
        cmds = [x for x in s["ins"] if x[1] in ("CMD", "ENTRYPOINT")]
        for kind in ("CMD", "ENTRYPOINT"):
            k = [x for x in cmds if x[1] == kind]
            if len(k) > 1:
                add("warn", "multiple-cmd", k[-1][0], f"{len(k)} {kind} instructions in one stage; only the last one counts",
                    f"keep a single {kind}")
        copied_all = None
        for ln, ins, args in s["ins"]:
            low = args.lower()
            if ins in ("ENV", "ARG"):
                pairs = re.findall(r"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?:(?:=|\s+)(\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\s=]\S*))?", args) if ins == "ARG" or "=" in args else [tuple((args.split(None, 1) + [""])[:2])]
                for key, val in pairs:
                    if SECRET_KEY.search(key) and val and not val.startswith("$") and val.strip("\"'"):
                        add("high", "secret-in-env", ln, f"{ins} {key} contains a literal secret; it is stored in the image layers and history",
                            "pass secrets at build time with RUN --mount=type=secret, or at run time via environment or a secrets manager")
                if ins == "ARG" and any(SECRET_KEY.search(k) for k, _ in pairs) and not any(v for k, v in pairs if SECRET_KEY.search(k)):
                    add("warn", "secret-in-env", ln, f"ARG {pairs[0][0]} looks like a secret; build args are visible in image history",
                        "use RUN --mount=type=secret instead of a build arg")
            if ins == "RUN":
                run_count += 1
                if re.search(r"(curl|wget)\b[^|;&]*\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(ba|z|da)?sh\b", low):
                    add("high", "curl-pipe-shell", ln, "downloads a script and pipes it straight into a shell",
                        "download to a file, verify a checksum or signature, then run it")
                if re.search(r"chmod\s+(-r\s+)?0?777\b", low):
                    add("high", "chmod-777", ln, "chmod 777 makes files writable by every user", "grant only the permissions needed, e.g. chmod 755 or chown to the app user")
                if re.search(r"(--password[= ]\S+|://[^/\s:@]+:[^@\s$]+@)", args) or re.search(r"\b(token|api[_-]?key)=\w{8,}", low):
                    add("high", "secret-in-run", ln, "a password, token, or credentials URL appears in a RUN command and stays in the image history",
                        "use RUN --mount=type=secret or fetch credentials at run time")
                if re.search(r"\bsudo\b", low):
                    add("warn", "sudo", ln, "sudo inside a Dockerfile is unnecessary and widens the attack surface", "run the step before switching USER, without sudo")
                for upd, inst in (("apt-get update", "apt-get install"), ("apt update", "apt install"), ("apk update", "apk add"), ("yum update", "yum install")):
                    if upd in low and inst not in low:
                        add("warn", "update-alone", ln, f"'{upd}' runs in its own layer; a later install may use a stale cached index",
                            f"combine: RUN {upd} && {inst} ... in one RUN")
                if "apt-get install" in low or "apt install" in low:
                    if "--no-install-recommends" not in low:
                        add("info", "apt-recommends", ln, "apt installs recommended packages too", "add --no-install-recommends")
                    if "/var/lib/apt/lists" not in low:
                        add("info", "apt-lists", ln, "apt package lists are left in the layer (tens of MB)", "end the same RUN with && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*")
                if "apk add" in low and "--no-cache" not in low:
                    add("info", "apk-cache", ln, "apk cache is kept in the layer", "use apk add --no-cache")
                if re.search(r"\bpip3?\s+install\b", low) and "--no-cache-dir" not in low and "--mount=type=cache" not in low:
                    add("info", "pip-cache", ln, "pip keeps its download cache in the layer", "add --no-cache-dir (or use a cache mount)")
                if any(re.fullmatch(r"\s*npm\s+(install|i)(\s+--?(?!g\b|global\b)[\w-]+(=\S+)?)*\s*", seg) for seg in re.split(r"&&|;|\|\|", low)):
                    add("info", "npm-ci", ln, "npm install can change the lockfile and versions", "use npm ci (with --omit=dev for production)")
                if re.match(r"cd\s+\S+\s*&&", low) or re.search(r"&&\s*cd\s+/", low):
                    add("info", "cd-in-run", ln, "cd in RUN only affects that one command", "use WORKDIR /path")
                if copied_all and re.search(r"\b(npm (ci|install)|pip3? install -r|poetry install|bundle install|go mod download|composer install|yarn install)\b", low):
                    add("warn", "cache-bust", ln, f"dependencies are installed after 'COPY {copied_all[1]}' (line {copied_all[0]}), so any source change reinstalls them",
                        "copy only the manifest and lockfile first (e.g. COPY package*.json ./), install, then COPY the rest")
                    copied_all = None
            if ins == "ADD":
                src = args.split()[0] if args.split() else ""
                if re.match(r"https?://", src):
                    add("warn", "use-copy", ln, "ADD with a URL downloads without checksum verification and leaves the file in a layer",
                        "use RUN curl -fsSL ... with a checksum check, or ADD --checksum=sha256:...")
                elif not re.search(r"\.(tar|tar\.gz|tgz|tar\.xz|tar\.bz2)$", src):
                    add("warn", "use-copy", ln, "ADD is used for local files; it also auto-extracts archives and fetches URLs", "use COPY for plain files")
            if ins == "COPY" and not args.startswith("--from"):
                parts = [p for p in args.split() if not p.startswith("--")]
                if parts and parts[0] in (".", "./", "*"):
                    copied_all = (ln, " ".join(parts))
                    add("info", "dockerignore", ln, "COPY of the whole build context", "make sure .dockerignore excludes .git, node_modules, .env, build output, and secrets")
            if ins == "EXPOSE" and re.search(r"\b22\b", args):
                add("warn", "ssh-port", ln, "port 22 (SSH) is exposed; containers should not run an SSH server", "use docker exec / kubectl exec for access")
            if ins in ("CMD", "ENTRYPOINT") and not args.strip().startswith("["):
                add("info", "shell-form", ln, f"shell-form {ins} runs under /bin/sh -c, so the app is not PID 1 and may miss SIGTERM",
                    f'use exec form: {ins} ["executable", "arg"]')

    users = [(ln, a.strip()) for ln, i, a in final["ins"] if i == "USER"]
    if not users or users[-1][1].split(":")[0] in ("root", "0"):
        where = users[-1][0] if users else final["line"]
        add("high", "root-user", where, "the final image runs as root",
            "create an unprivileged user (e.g. RUN useradd -r -u 10001 app) and add USER app before CMD")
    if not any(i == "HEALTHCHECK" for _, i, _ in final["ins"]):
        add("info", "no-healthcheck", final["line"], "no HEALTHCHECK in the final stage", "add HEALTHCHECK CMD ... if no orchestrator health probe is configured")
    if len(stages) == 1 and any(BUILD_TOOLS.search(a) for _, i, a in final["ins"] if i == "RUN"):
        add("info", "single-stage", final["line"], "build tools are installed in the only stage, so they ship in the final image",
            "use a multi-stage build: compile in a builder stage, COPY --from=builder only the output")
    if run_count > 10:
        add("info", "many-layers", final["line"], f"{run_count} RUN instructions; related steps can be combined", "group related commands with && in fewer RUN steps")
    return {"stages": [{"line": s["line"], "image": s["image"], "name": s["name"]} for s in stages], "findings": findings}


def main(argv):
    as_json, fail_on, files = False, "high", []
    it = iter(argv)
    for a in it:
        if a == "--json":
            as_json = True
        elif a == "--fail-on":
            fail_on = next(it, "").lower()
            if fail_on not in LEVELS:
                print("error: --fail-on must be high, warn, or info", file=sys.stderr)
                return 2
        elif a in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(__doc__)
            return 0
        elif a.startswith("--"):
            print(f"error: unknown option {a}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        else:
            files.append(a)
    if not files:
        print("error: give a Dockerfile path, or - for stdin", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    reports, worst = [], -1
    for f in files:
        try:
            text = sys.stdin.read() if f == "-" else open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
            r = review(text)
        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
            print(f"error: {f}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        r["file"] = f
        r["findings"].sort(key=lambda x: (-LEVELS[x["level"]], x["line"]))
        for x in r["findings"]:
            worst = max(worst, LEVELS[x["level"]])
        reports.append(r)
    if as_json:
        print(json.dumps(reports, indent=2))
    else:
        for r in reports:
            c = {lv: sum(1 for x in r["findings"] if x["level"] == lv) for lv in LEVELS}
            st = ", ".join(f"{s['image']}" + (f" AS {s['name']}" if s["name"] else "") for s in r["stages"])
            print(f"{r['file']}: {len(r['stages'])} stage(s): {st}")
            print(f"  HIGH {c['high']}  WARN {c['warn']}  INFO {c['info']}")
            for x in r["findings"]:
                print(f"  {x['level'].upper():<4} line {x['line']:<3} {x['rule']:<15} {x['message']}")
                print(f"       fix: {x['fix']}")
            if not r["findings"]:
                print("  no problems found")
    return 1 if worst >= LEVELS[fail_on] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

# Regex Pattern Explainer and Tester

You help people understand, fix, and trust regular expressions. You explain a pattern in plain words, prove what it does with real test cases, and find the traps that make regexes fail in production: inputs that should not pass, inputs that should pass but do not, and patterns that hang on long input. You return a corrected pattern with a test table, not just an opinion.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/regex_check.py` - explains a pattern from Python's own regex parser, runs sample inputs with "+" (must match) and "-" (must not match) expectations, and reports HIGH, WARN, and INFO risks; `--probe` times the pattern on generated worst-case input in a subprocess (Python 3 standard library only)
- `references/regex-pitfalls.md` - every risk the checker reports, why it matters, and the safe pattern to use instead
- `references/flavor-differences.md` - how Python `re` differs from JavaScript, PCRE, Go RE2, .NET, Java, and POSIX grep, so a fix works where the user runs it
- `templates/regex-review.md` - the review report to return
- `examples/example-email-validation-review.md` - a worked review of an email check that hangs on long input

## Workflow

### 1. Collect the facts
Ask, or assume and say so:
- The pattern exactly as written in the code (raw string or escaped string literal) and the language or tool that runs it.
- What it must accept and what it must reject: 4 to 10 real examples of each, including edge cases (empty input, spaces, Unicode, very long input).
- How it is used: validate a whole value (fullmatch), find the first match (search), extract all matches (findall), or replace.
- Where the input comes from. Untrusted input (web forms, logs, API payloads) makes catastrophic backtracking a security issue.

### 2. Run the checker
```bash

python3 scripts/regex_check.py 'PATTERN' --cases cases.txt --mode fullmatch --flags a
python3 scripts/regex_check.py 'PATTERN' --probe --no-explain         # confirm a backtracking risk
python3 scripts/regex_check.py 'PATTERN' --cases - --json < cases.txt
```
A cases file has one sample per line: `+ text` must match, `- text` must not match, `# ...` is a comment. Always quote the pattern in single quotes in the shell. The checker uses Python's `re`; for other flavors, read `references/flavor-differences.md` and translate the result. If you cannot run the script, explain the pattern by hand with the same structure and apply `references/regex-pitfalls.md`.

### 3. Explain, then fix
1. Explain the pattern top to bottom in plain words, one line per token or group, using the checker's explanation as the base.
2. Show the test table: each sample, expected result, actual result, and the matched text or groups.
3. Fix in this order: patterns that can hang (HIGH), wrong accepts and wrong rejects (failed expectations), then clarity and the INFO notes.
4. Prefer simple, readable rewrites: one repeat instead of nested ones, negated classes like `[^,]*` instead of `.*`, explicit anchors `\A...\Z` or `fullmatch`, and `re.VERBOSE` with comments for long patterns.
5. Rerun the checker on the corrected pattern with the same cases plus any new edge cases until every expectation passes and there is no HIGH risk. Run `--probe` on the fix if the original had a HIGH risk.

### 4. Deliver
Fill in `templates/regex-review.md`: the plain-language explanation, the test table before and after, the risks found, the corrected pattern in the user's language with correct escaping, and a short list of test cases to keep in their test suite. # Regex pitfalls checked by the script

Each rule: what is detected, why it matters, and the pattern to use instead. Levels: HIGH can hang or be exploited, WARN usually accepts or rejects the wrong input, INFO is a habit worth fixing.

## HIGH (catastrophic backtracking, ReDoS)

### nested-quantifier
Detected: a repeat inside another repeat where nothing else in the outer repeat is required, such as `(a+)+`, `(\w+\s?)+`, `([a-z0-9]+\.?)+`, `(\w+|\d+)+`.
Why: on input that almost matches (a long run of letters followed by a char the pattern rejects), the engine tries every way to split the run between the inner and outer repeat: 2^n ways for n chars. 30 chars can take minutes. On a web form or API this is a denial-of-service bug.
Use instead: one repeat that describes the whole run, with the separator required.
```
(\w+\s?)+$          ->  \w+(?:\s\w+)*$
([a-z0-9]+\.?)+@    ->  [a-z0-9]+(?:\.[a-z0-9]+)*@
```
Python 3.11+ also supports atomic groups `(?>...)` and possessive quantifiers `a++`, which never give back what they matched.

### ambiguous-repeat
Detected: a repeat whose body has variable length and whose required parts can also be eaten by the variable part, such as `(x+x+)+`, `(aa|a)+`, `(foo|f\w+)+`.
Why: same as above, the iterations can be cut in many ways. Growth may be slower (Fibonacci instead of 2^n) but is still exponential.
Use instead: make each iteration start with a char nothing else in the body can match, or merge the parts into one class.

Confirm both with `--probe`: the script runs the pattern on `c * n + tail` for n = 12 to 28 in a subprocess with a 2 second limit and reports how fast the time grows. A growth of more than 3x per 4 extra chars, or a timeout, confirms the risk.

## WARN

### nested-overlap
A repeat whose body has a separator that the inner part also accepts, such as `([\w.]+\.)+`. Make the inner class exclude the separator: `(?:[\w-]+\.)+`.

### adjacent-overlap
Two unbounded single-char repeats in a row that accept the same chars, such as `\d+\d+` or `.*.*`. The split point is ambiguous and a failing match backtracks polynomially (n^2, n^3). Keep one of them or make the boundary explicit.

### range-A-z
`[A-z]` covers ASCII 65 to 122, which includes `[ \ ] ^ _` and the backtick. Use `[A-Za-z]`, or `[^\W\d_]` for any Unicode letter.

### unescaped-dot
`.` between letters or before a word such as `com` or `json` matches any char, so `example-com` passes a check for `example.com`. Write `\.`.

### matches-empty
The pattern accepts the empty string. A validation then accepts blank input, and `findall` returns empty strings between real matches. Use `+` instead of `*` where at least one char is required.

## INFO

### not-anchored
`re.search(r"\d+", "abc123xyz")` succeeds. For validating a whole value, use `re.fullmatch` or anchor with `\A ... \Z`.

### dollar-newline
`$` matches at the end of the string and also just before a final newline, so `^abc$` accepts `"abc\n"` with `re.search` or `re.match`. Use `\Z` or `re.fullmatch` for strict checks.

### unicode-classes
In Python 3, `\d` matches any Unicode digit (for example Arabic-Indic digits) and `\w` matches letters in every script. Good for names and free text; for IDs, card numbers, and codes use `re.ASCII` or `[0-9]`.

### greedy-dotstar and many-dotstar
`.*` takes everything and then gives back one char at a time. Three or more `.*` in one pattern make failures slow on long lines. Describe each field with a negated class: `"[^"]*"` for a quoted string, `[^,]*` for a CSV field.

## Not detected by the script (check by hand)

- Wrong escaping in the host language (a Python string without `r""`, a Java string with single backslashes).
- Business rules a regex cannot express well: valid dates (February 30), checksums (IBAN, card numbers), real email deliverability.
- Locale issues: case-insensitive matching of Turkish dotted and dotless i, German sharp s.
- Performance of huge alternations (thousands of words): use a set lookup or a trie instead.

# Regex flavor differences that break fixes

The checker runs Python `re`. Before handing a pattern to another engine, check this table.

| Feature | Python `re` | JavaScript | PCRE / PHP | Go (RE2) | .NET | Java | POSIX grep -E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lookahead `(?=...)` | yes | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | no |
| Lookbehind `(?<=...)` | fixed width only | yes (ES2018) | fixed or bounded | no | any width | bounded | no |
| Named group | `(?P<name>...)` only | `(?<name>...)` | both | `(?P<name>...)` (also `(?<name>...)` in Go 1.22+) | `(?<name>...)` | `(?<name>...)` | no |
| Atomic group `(?>...)` | 3.11+ | no | yes | no | yes | yes | no |
| Possessive `a++` | 3.11+ | no | yes | no | no | yes | no |
| Backreference `\1` | yes | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes (basic) |
| `\d` matches non-ASCII digits | yes (unless re.ASCII) | no | no (unless UCP) | no | yes | no (unless UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS) | locale |
| `$` before final newline | yes | no (without m flag) | yes | no | yes | yes | n/a (line based) |
| Inline flags `(?i)` | yes, at start or scoped `(?i:...)` | flags after the literal (`/i`); scoped `(?i:...)` only in the newest engines | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| Catastrophic backtracking | possible | possible | possible (has limits) | impossible (linear time) | possible (timeout option) | possible | engine dependent |
| Full match helper | `re.fullmatch` | anchor with `^...$` | anchor | anchor | anchor | `String.matches()` | `-x` flag |

## Translation notes

- JavaScript: write the literal as `/pattern/flags`; escape `/` inside it. Use the `u` flag for Unicode and `v` for set operations in newer engines. `\Z` does not exist: use `$` without the `m` flag.
- Go RE2: no lookarounds or backreferences, but every pattern runs in linear time, so ReDoS is not a concern there. Rewrite lookarounds as a second check in code.
- Java and C#: every backslash doubles in a normal string literal (`"\\d+"`); C# verbatim strings `@"\d+"` and Java text blocks help.
- .NET: set `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` (.NET 7+) or a match timeout for untrusted input.
- SQL: PostgreSQL `~` uses Tcl-style advanced regexes (lookahead, lookbehind since 9.6, no named groups); MySQL 8 uses ICU. Test in the database itself.
- Shell: `grep -E` has no `\d` on many systems; use `[0-9]`. `grep -P` gives PCRE where available.

## Safe defaults across flavors

- `[0-9]` instead of `\d`, `[A-Za-z]` instead of `\w` when the format is ASCII by definition.
- Anchors `^` and `$` without multiline mode, plus a separate length check (for example at most 254 chars for an email).
- No nested quantifiers on untrusted input, whatever the engine.

    for op, av in items:
        name = op_name(op)
        if name == "LITERAL":
            parts.append(show_char(av))
        elif name == "RANGE":
            parts.append(f"{show_char(av[0])}-{show_char(av[1])}")
        elif name == "CATEGORY":
            parts.append(CATEGORY_TEXT.get(op_name(av), op_name(av)))
    return ("any char except " if negate else "one of: ") + ", ".join(parts)


def explain(seq, group_names, flags, depth=0, out=None):
    out = [] if out is None else out
    pad = "  " * depth
    i = 0
    while i < len(seq):
        op, av = seq[i]
        name = op_name(op)
        if name == "LITERAL":  # merge runs of literals
            j = i
            while j < len(seq) and op_name(seq[j][0]) == "LITERAL":
                j += 1
            text = "".join(chr(a) for _, a in seq[i:j])
            out.append(f"{pad}the text {text!r}" if j - i > 1 else f"{pad}the char {show_char(av)}")
            i = j
            continue
        if name == "NOT_LITERAL":
            out.append(f"{pad}any char except {show_char(av)}")
        elif name == "IN":
            out.append(f"{pad}{class_text(av)}")
        elif name == "ANY":
            out.append(f"{pad}any char" + ("" if flags & re.DOTALL else " except newline"))
        elif name == "AT":
            out.append(f"{pad}{AT_TEXT.get(op_name(av), op_name(av))}")
        elif name in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT", "POSSESSIVE_REPEAT"):
            lo, hi, sub = av
            out.append(f"{pad}{quant_text(lo, hi, name)} of:")
            explain(sub, group_names, flags, depth + 1, out)
        elif name == "SUBPATTERN":
            g = av[0]
            if g is None:
                out.append(f"{pad}non-capturing group:")
            else:
                label = f' "{group_names[g]}"' if g in group_names else ""
                out.append(f"{pad}capturing group {g}{label}:")
            explain(av[3], group_names, flags_for(av, flags), depth + 1, out)
        elif name == "ATOMIC_GROUP":
            out.append(f"{pad}atomic group (no backtracking into it):")
            explain(av, group_names, flags, depth + 1, out)
        elif name == "BRANCH":
            out.append(f"{pad}either:")
            for k, b in enumerate(av[1]):
                out.append(f"{pad}  option {k + 1}:")
                explain(b, group_names, flags, depth + 2, out)
        elif name in ("ASSERT", "ASSERT_NOT"):
            direction, sub = av
            kind = ("lookbehind" if direction < 0 else "lookahead")
            neg = "negative " if name == "ASSERT_NOT" else ""
            out.append(f"{pad}{neg}{kind} (checks without consuming):")
            explain(sub, group_names, flags, depth + 1, out)
        elif name == "GROUPREF":
            out.append(f"{pad}the same text as group {av} matched")
        elif name == "GROUPREF_EXISTS":
            out.append(f"{pad}if group {av[0]} matched:")
            explain(av[1], group_names, flags, depth + 1, out)
            if av[2]:
                out.append(f"{pad}otherwise:")
                explain(av[2], group_names, flags, depth + 1, out)
        else:
            out.append(f"{pad}{name}")
        i += 1
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- risk analysis

def walk_repeats(seq, flags, path=""):
    """Yield (op, av, flags) for every repeat node, outside lookarounds too."""
    for op, av in seq:
        name = op_name(op)
        if name in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT", "POSSESSIVE_REPEAT"):
            yield op, av, flags
            yield from walk_repeats(av[2], flags)
        elif name == "SUBPATTERN":
            yield from walk_repeats(av[3], flags_for(av, flags))
        elif name == "ATOMIC_GROUP":
            yield from walk_repeats(av, flags)
        elif name == "BRANCH":
            for b in av[1]:
                yield from walk_repeats(b, flags)
        elif name in ("ASSERT", "ASSERT_NOT"):
            yield from walk_repeats(av[1], flags)


def flatten(seq):
    """Expand groups so the body of a repeat can be read as one token list."""
    out = []
    for op, av in seq:
        name = op_name(op)
        if name == "SUBPATTERN" and av[1] == 0 and av[2] == 0:
            out.extend(flatten(av[3]))
        else:
            out.append((op, av))
    return out


def token_width(tok, parsed):
    return sre_parse.SubPattern(parsed.state, [tok]).getwidth()


def all_chars(seq, flags):
    """Every ALPHABET char a token sequence can consume anywhere (not only first)."""
    acc = set()
    for op, av in seq:
        name = op_name(op)
        if name in ("LITERAL", "NOT_LITERAL", "IN", "ANY"):
            acc |= token_first(op, av, flags)[0]
        elif name in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT", "POSSESSIVE_REPEAT"):
            acc |= all_chars(av[2], flags)
        elif name == "SUBPATTERN":
            acc |= all_chars(av[3], flags_for(av, flags))
        elif name == "ATOMIC_GROUP":
            acc |= all_chars(av, flags)
        elif name == "BRANCH":
            for b in av[1]:
                acc |= all_chars(b, flags)
        elif name == "GROUPREF_EXISTS":
            acc |= all_chars(av[1], flags) | all_chars(av[2] or [], flags)
        elif name == "GROUPREF":
            acc |= set(ALPHABET)
    return acc


def has_unbounded(tok):
    op, av = tok
    name = op_name(op)
    if name in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT"):
        return av[1] == MAXREPEAT or has_unbounded_seq(av[2])
    if name == "SUBPATTERN":
        return has_unbounded_seq(av[3])
    if name == "BRANCH":
        return any(has_unbounded_seq(b) for b in av[1])
    return False


def has_unbounded_seq(seq):
    return any(has_unbounded(t) for t in seq)


def sample_char(chars):
    for pool in (string.ascii_lowercase, string.digits, string.ascii_uppercase, ALPHABET):
        for c in pool:
            if c in chars:
                return c
    return None


def analyze(parsed, flags, pattern, modes_seen):
    risks = []

    def add(level, rule, msg, probe=None):
        risks.append({"level": level, "rule": rule, "message": msg, **({"probe": probe} if probe else {})})

    # nested quantifiers: a repeat whose body can match the same text in more than one way
    for op, av, fl in walk_repeats(list(parsed), flags):
        if op_name(op) == "POSSESSIVE_REPEAT" or av[1] <= 1:
            continue
        body = flatten(av[2])
        widths = [token_width(t, parsed) for t in body]
        if sum(w[0] for w in widths) == sum(w[1] for w in widths):
            continue  # fixed-width body such as (\d{4}-)+ cannot be split two ways
        variable = [t for t, w in zip(body, widths) if w[0] != w[1]]
        fixed = [t for t, w in zip(body, widths) if w[0] == w[1] and w[0] > 0]
        var_chars = set().union(*(all_chars([t], fl) for t in variable))
        has_inner_loop = any(has_unbounded(t) for t in variable)
        overlap = set().union(*(all_chars([t], fl) for t in fixed)) & var_chars if fixed else set()
        sample = sample_char(overlap) or sample_char(var_chars)
        if not fixed and has_inner_loop:
            add("high", "nested-quantifier",
                "a quantifier sits inside another quantifier and nothing else in the outer repeat is "
                "required (the classic (a+)+ or (\\w+\\s?)+ shape), so one string can be split in "
                "exponentially many ways; rewrite as a single repeat, make the separator required, or use an "
                "atomic group or possessive quantifier (Python 3.11+)", probe=sample)
        elif any(not (all_chars([t], fl) & var_chars) for t in fixed):
            if has_inner_loop:
                add("info", "nested-separated",
                    "nested quantifier with a required separator that the inner repeat cannot match "
                    "(like ([\\w-]+\\.)+); this shape is safe")
        elif all(all_chars([t], fl) <= var_chars for t in fixed):
            add("high", "ambiguous-repeat",
                "the body of a repeat has variable length and every required part can also be eaten by "
                "the variable part (for example (x+x+)+, (aa|a)+, or (\\w+|\\d+)+), so the iterations "
                "can be split in exponentially many ways; merge the parts into one class or make each "
                "iteration start with a char the rest cannot match", probe=sample)
        else:
            add("warn", "nested-overlap",
                "a repeat with a variable-length body whose separator is also accepted by the inner part "
                "(for example ([\\w.]+\\.)+): long non-matching input can slow down sharply; make the inner "
                "class exclude the separator", probe=sample)

    # adjacent overlapping unbounded repeats in any sequence
    seen_pairs = set()

    def single_char_repeat(op, av):
        return (op_name(op) in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT") and av[1] == MAXREPEAT and len(av[2]) == 1
                and op_name(av[2][0][0]) in ("LITERAL", "NOT_LITERAL", "IN", "ANY"))

    def scan_adjacent(seq, fl):
        toks = [t for t in flatten(seq) if op_name(t[0]) not in ("AT", "ASSERT", "ASSERT_NOT")]
        for (a_op, a_av), (b_op, b_av) in zip(toks, toks[1:]):
            if single_char_repeat(a_op, a_av) and single_char_repeat(b_op, b_av):
                if (id(a_av), id(b_av)) in seen_pairs:
                    continue
                seen_pairs.add((id(a_av), id(b_av)))
                fa, _ = first_info(a_av[2], fl)
                fb, _ = first_info(b_av[2], fl)
                if fa & fb:
                    add("warn", "adjacent-overlap",
                        "two unbounded quantifiers in a row accept the same chars (for example \\d+\\d+ or "
                        ".*.*), so the split between them is ambiguous and failures backtrack polynomially; "
                        "keep one of them")
        for op, av in seq:
            name = op_name(op)
            if name == "SUBPATTERN":
                scan_adjacent(av[3], flags_for(av, fl))
            elif name in ("MAX_REPEAT", "MIN_REPEAT", "POSSESSIVE_REPEAT"):
                scan_adjacent(av[2], fl)
            elif name == "BRANCH":
                for b in av[1]:
                    scan_adjacent(b, fl)

    scan_adjacent(list(parsed), flags)

    # text-level checks
    if re.search(r"\[[^\]]*A-z", pattern):
        add("warn", "range-A-z", "[A-z] also matches [ \\ ] ^ _ and the backtick; use [A-Za-z]")
    seq = list(parsed)
    flat = flatten(seq)
    for k, (op, _av) in enumerate(flat):
        if op_name(op) != "ANY":
            continue
        before = flat[k - 1] if k else None
        after = [chr(a) for o, a in flat[k + 1:k + 4] if op_name(o) == "LITERAL"]
        lit_before = before is not None and op_name(before[0]) == "LITERAL" and chr(before[1]).isalnum()
        word_after = len(after) >= 2 and all(c.isalpha() for c in after[:2])
        if (lit_before and after and after[0].isalnum()) or word_after:
            add("warn", "unescaped-dot",
                f"'.' before {''.join(after) or 'the next token'!r} matches any char (so a '-' or 'x' passes there too); "
                "write \\. for a literal dot")
            break
    try:
        if re.compile(pattern, flags).fullmatch(""):
            add("warn", "matches-empty",
                "the pattern matches the empty string, so findall/finditer return empty matches and "
                "validation accepts blank input; require at least one char where it matters")
    except re.error:
        pass
    count_dotstar = len(re.findall(r"(?<!\\)\.\*", pattern))
    if count_dotstar >= 3:
        add("info", "many-dotstar", f"{count_dotstar} '.*' in one pattern: failures are slow on long lines; "
            "use negated classes like [^,]* to describe each field")
    elif count_dotstar and not re.search(r"\.\*\?", pattern):
        add("info", "greedy-dotstar", "greedy .* grabs as much as possible and then backs off; use .*? or a "
            "negated class such as [^\"]* when you mean 'up to the next ...'")
    first_ops = [op_name(op) for op, _ in seq[:1]]
    last = seq[-1] if seq else None
    anchored_start = first_ops == ["AT"]
    anchored_end = last is not None and op_name(last[0]) == "AT" and op_name(last[1]) in ("AT_END", "AT_END_STRING")
    if "fullmatch" not in modes_seen and not (anchored_start and anchored_end) and modes_seen != {"findall"}:
        add("info", "not-anchored", "for validation, anchor both ends (\\A ... \\Z) or use re.fullmatch; "
            "otherwise 'abc123xyz' passes a search for \\d+")
    if anchored_end and op_name(last[1]) == "AT_END" and not flags & re.MULTILINE and "fullmatch" not in modes_seen:
        add("info", "dollar-newline", "$ also matches before a trailing newline ('abc\\n' passes ^abc$); "
            "use \\Z or fullmatch for strict validation")
    if re.search(r"(?<!\\)\\[dw]", pattern) and not flags & re.ASCII:
        add("info", "unicode-classes", "\\d and \\w match Unicode digits and letters too (for example "
            "Arabic-Indic digits); add re.ASCII or use [0-9] / [A-Za-z0-9_] for strict input formats")
    return risks


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- probe

PROBE_CODE = r"""
import re, sys, time
pat, flags, s = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
rx = re.compile(pat, flags)
t = time.perf_counter(); rx.search(s); print(f"{time.perf_counter() - t:.6f}")
"""


def run_probe(pattern, flags, ch, compiled):
    tail = next((t for t in "!#\x00~ \n" if not compiled.search(ch * 3 + t)), "!")
    results, verdict = [], "no slowdown seen"
    for n in (12, 16, 20, 24, 28):
        s = ch * n + tail
        try:
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", PROBE_CODE, pattern, str(flags), s],
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=2)
            secs = float(r.stdout.strip() or "nan")
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            results.append({"n": n, "seconds": None})
            verdict = f"TIMEOUT at length {n + 1}: exponential backtracking confirmed"
            break
        results.append({"n": n, "seconds": round(secs, 4)})
        prev = results[-2]["seconds"] if len(results) >= 2 else None
        if prev and secs > 0.01 and secs / prev > 3:
            verdict = (f"time grows about {secs / prev:.0f}x per +4 chars: exponential backtracking confirmed")
        elif secs > 0.5:
            verdict = f"slow ({secs:.2f} s at length {n + 1}) but not clearly exponential"
    return {"input": f"{ch!r} * n + {tail!r}", "timings": results, "verdict": verdict}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- matching

def read_cases(path):
    text = sys.stdin.read() if path == "-" else open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    cases = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        if raw.startswith("+ ") or raw.startswith("- "):
            cases.append({"text": raw[2:], "expect": raw[0] == "+"})
        else:
            cases.append({"text": raw, "expect": None})
    return cases


def match_case(rx, text, mode):
    fn = {"search": rx.search, "match": rx.match, "fullmatch": rx.fullmatch}.get(mode)
    names = {v: k for k, v in rx.groupindex.items()}
    def groups(m):
        out = []
        for g in range(1, rx.groups + 1):
            out.append({"group": g, "name": names.get(g), "value": m.group(g),
                        "span": list(m.span(g)) if m.group(g) is not None else None})
        return out
    if mode == "findall":
        ms = list(rx.finditer(text))
        return {"matched": bool(ms), "matches": [{"text": m.group(0), "span": list(m.span()), "groups": groups(m)}
                                                for m in ms]}
    m = fn(text)
    if not m:
        return {"matched": False, "matches": []}
    return {"matched": True, "matches": [{"text": m.group(0), "span": list(m.span()), "groups": groups(m)}]}


def describe_flags(flags):
    names = [n for f, n in FLAG_NAMES if flags & f]
    return ", ".join(names) if names else "none"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main

def parse_args(argv):
    opts = {"texts": [], "cases": None, "mode": "search", "flags": 0, "probe": False, "explain": True,
            "json": False, "fail_on": "high", "pattern": None, "timeout": 2.0}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        def val():
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                raise UsageError(f"{a} needs a value")
            return argv[i + 1]
        if a in ("-t", "--text"):
            opts["texts"].append(val()); i += 2
        elif a == "--cases":
            opts["cases"] = val(); i += 2
        elif a == "--mode":
            opts["mode"] = val(); i += 2
            if opts["mode"] not in ("search", "match", "fullmatch", "findall"):
                raise UsageError("--mode must be search, match, fullmatch, or findall")
        elif a == "--flags":
            letters = val(); i += 2
            bad = [c for c in letters.lower() if c not in FLAG_LETTERS]
            if bad:
                raise UsageError(f"unknown flag letter(s) {''.join(bad)!r}; use any of i m s x a")
            for c in letters.lower():
                opts["flags"] |= FLAG_LETTERS[c]
        elif a == "--fail-on":
            opts["fail_on"] = val().lower(); i += 2
            if opts["fail_on"] not in ("high", "warn", "info", "never"):
                raise UsageError("--fail-on must be high, warn, info, or never")
        elif a == "--timeout":
            try:
                opts["timeout"] = float(val())
            except ValueError:
                raise UsageError("--timeout needs a number of seconds, for example --timeout 2")
            i += 2
        elif a == "--probe":
            opts["probe"] = True; i += 1
        elif a == "--no-explain":
            opts["explain"] = False; i += 1
        elif a == "--json":
            opts["json"] = True; i += 1
        elif a in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(__doc__); sys.exit(0)
        elif a.startswith("--") and opts["pattern"] is not None:
            raise UsageError(f"unknown option {a}")
        elif opts["pattern"] is None:
            opts["pattern"] = a; i += 1
        else:
            raise UsageError(f"unexpected argument {a!r} (quote the pattern; use -t for sample inputs)")
    if opts["pattern"] is None:
        raise UsageError("give a PATTERN (quote it in single quotes in the shell)")
    return opts


def main(argv):
    try:
        opts = parse_args(argv)
        cases = [{"text": t, "expect": None} for t in opts["texts"]]
        if opts["cases"]:
            try:
                cases += read_cases(opts["cases"])
            except OSError as e:
                raise UsageError(f"cannot read cases file: {e.strerror}: {opts['cases']}")
    except UsageError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    pattern, flags, mode = opts["pattern"], opts["flags"], opts["mode"]
    try:
        rx = re.compile(pattern, flags)
        parsed = sre_parse.parse(pattern, flags)
    except re.error as e:
        pos = f" at position {e.pos}" if e.pos is not None else ""
        print(f"error: pattern does not compile: {e.msg}{pos}", file=sys.stderr)
        if e.pos is not None:
            print(f"  {pattern}\n  {' ' * e.pos}^", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    flags = int(rx.flags) & ~int(re.UNICODE)
    names = {v: k for k, v in rx.groupindex.items()}
    risks = analyze(parsed, flags, pattern, {mode})
    if opts["probe"]:
        for r in risks:
            if r.get("probe"):
                r["probe_result"] = run_probe(pattern, flags, r["probe"], rx)
    results = []
    for c in cases:
        try:
            res = with_timeout(opts["timeout"], match_case, rx, c["text"], mode)
            status = None if c["expect"] is None else ("PASS" if res["matched"] == c["expect"] else "FAIL")
        except MatchTimeout:
            res, status = {"matched": None, "matches": []}, "TIMEOUT"
        results.append({**c, **res, "status": status})
    fails = sum(1 for r in results if r["status"] in ("FAIL", "TIMEOUT"))
    counts = {lvl: sum(1 for r in risks if r["level"] == lvl) for lvl in ("high", "warn", "info")}
    report = {"pattern": pattern, "flags": describe_flags(flags), "mode": mode, "groups": rx.groups,
              "group_names": {str(k): v for k, v in names.items()},
              "explanation": explain(list(parsed), names, flags) if opts["explain"] else [],
              "cases": results, "failed_expectations": fails, "risks": risks, "risk_counts": counts}
    threshold = LEVELS.get(opts["fail_on"], 99)
    risky = any(LEVELS[r["level"]] >= threshold for r in risks)
    if opts["json"]:
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1 if fails or risky else 0

    print(f"Pattern: {pattern}")
    named = ", ".join(f'{g} "{n}"' for g, n in sorted(names.items()))
    print(f"Flags: {describe_flags(flags)} | mode: {mode} | groups: {rx.groups}" + (f" ({named})" if named else ""))
    if opts["explain"]:
        print("\nExplanation:")
        for line in report["explanation"]:
            print("  " + line)
    if results:
        print(f"\nSamples ({mode}):")
        for r in results:
            mark = {True: "+", False: "-", None: " "}[r["expect"]]
            tag = r["status"] or ("match" if r["matched"] else "no match")
            line = f"  {tag:<8} {mark} {r['text']!r}"
            if r["matched"]:
                parts = []
                for m in r["matches"][:5]:
                    g = " ".join(f"{x['name'] or x['group']}={x['value']!r}" for x in m["groups"])
                    parts.append(f"[{m['span'][0]}:{m['span'][1]}] {m['text']!r}" + (f" {g}" if g else ""))
                more = f" (+{len(r['matches']) - 5} more)" if len(r["matches"]) > 5 else ""
                line += "  -> " + "; ".join(parts) + more
            elif r["status"] == "TIMEOUT":
                line += f"  -> still running after {opts['timeout']:g} s (catastrophic backtracking)"
            elif r["status"] == "FAIL":
                line += "  -> expected a match"
            if r["status"] == "FAIL" and r["matched"]:
                line += "  (expected no match)"
            print(line)
    print("\nRisks and suggestions:")
    if not risks:
        print("  none found")
    for r in risks:
        print(f"  {r['level'].upper():<4} {r['rule']:<23} {r['message']}")
        pr = r.get("probe_result")
        if pr:
            times = ", ".join(f"n={t['n']}: {'timeout' if t['seconds'] is None else str(t['seconds']) + ' s'}"
                              for t in pr["timings"])
            print(f"       probe {pr['input']}: {times} -> {pr['verdict']}")
    summary = f"\nSummary: HIGH {counts['high']}  WARN {counts['warn']}  INFO {counts['info']}"
    if any(r["expect"] is not None for r in results):
        n = sum(1 for r in results if r["expect"] is not None)
        summary += f" | expectations {n - fails}/{n} pass"
    timeouts = sum(1 for r in results if r["status"] == "TIMEOUT")
    if timeouts:
        summary += f" | {timeouts} sample(s) timed out"
    print(summary)
    return 1 if fails or risky else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

You help podcasters turn a messy transcript into show notes that listeners actually read and search engines can find. You find the real structure of the conversation, name chapters the way a listener would describe them, choose quotes that work out of context, and write a summary that tells someone in two lines why this episode is worth their time. You never invent facts, links, or quotes that are not in the material.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/chapterize.py` - reads timestamped, WebVTT, headed, or plain transcripts, proposes chapter starts from headings, pause markers, cue phrases ("let's talk about", "after the break"), and vocabulary shifts, drafts keyword titles, lists ad and music markers, and ranks quote candidates (Python 3 standard library only)

- `templates/show-notes.md` - the show notes document to return
- `examples/example-rooftop-beekeeping-episode.md` - a worked example from a 25-minute interview

## Workflow

### 1. Collect the material
Ask, or assume and say so:
- The transcript (any format) and whether its times match the final edit. If an intro or ad was added after transcription, get the offset in seconds.
- Show name, host and guest names with correct spelling, the guest's role, and links they want included (only links the user gives you).
- Where the notes will be published (podcast host, YouTube, website, newsletter) and any house style: tone, length, emoji, sponsor wording.
- The audience and 2 or 3 search phrases a listener might type to find this episode.

### 2. Run the chapter finder
```bash
python3 scripts/chapterize.py transcript.txt
python3 scripts/chapterize.py transcript.txt --min-chapter 3 --offset 45 --duration 52:30
python3 scripts/chapterize.py episode.vtt --format youtube
python3 scripts/chapterize.py - --format json < transcript.txt
```
The script's chapter starts and quotes are candidates, not answers. Read the transcript around every proposed start and move it to the sentence where the new topic really begins. Rewrite every keyword title (for example "Roof / Hive / Water / Wind") into a short listener-facing title ("Keeping bees on a windy roof"). If there are no timestamps, times are estimates (marked `~`); tell the user to replace them with times from the audio editor. If you cannot run the script, find chapters by hand the same way: headings, breaks, transition phrases, then topic changes.

### 3. Write the notes
1. Title: 40 to 60 characters, the main promise of the episode, guest name if it helps search.
2. Summary: 2 sentences for the app preview (the first 150 characters must work alone), then one short paragraph.
3. Key takeaways: 3 to 5 bullets, each a concrete idea from the episode, not a topic name.
4. Chapters: 4 to 10 for a 20 to 60 minute episode, first at 00:00, titles under 40 characters, in the order they happen.
5. Quotes: 3 to 5 lines that make sense without context, with speaker and time. Remove filler words only; never change meaning. Mark edited quotes so the user can check them against the audio.
6. Guest bio (2 or 3 sentences), links and resources mentioned (only real ones from the material or the user), credits, sponsor disclosure if there was an ad.
7. Social posts: one per platform the user names, each with one quote or takeaway.

### 4. Deliver
Fill in `templates/show-notes.md` and follow `references/show-notes-structure.md` and `references/chapters-and-platforms.md`. Follow the style of `examples/example-rooftop-beekeeping-episode.md`. Add a short "check before publishing" list: estimated times, edited quotes, spellings, and any facts or numbers the guest stated that should be verified.

## Rules
- Only use facts, names, numbers, and links from the transcript or the user; flag anything unclear as [check].
- Quotes must be the speaker's own words; removing "um" and "you know" is fine, rewording is not.
- Keep chapter titles descriptive and honest; no clickbait the episode does not deliver.
- Respect guests: do not quote private remarks, off-the-record moments, or anything the user marks as cut.
- Match the show's voice; default to warm, clear, and specific.

# Show notes structure

Listeners skim show notes in a podcast app on a phone, search engines read them on the episode page, and the guest shares them. Each section has one job.

| Section | Job | Length |
|---|---|---|
| Episode title | Say the main promise; help search | 40 to 60 characters; most apps cut after about 60 |
| Preview summary | Make someone press play from the app list | First 150 characters must work alone; 2 sentences total |
| Full summary | Explain who the guest is and what you cover | 60 to 120 words |
| Key takeaways | Give skimmers the value | 3 to 5 bullets, one idea each, under 20 words |
| Chapters | Let listeners jump | 4 to 10 for 20 to 60 minutes; titles under 40 characters |
| Pull quotes | Quotable lines for notes and social | 3 to 5, 12 to 30 words each, with speaker and time |
| Guest bio | Credit the guest | 2 or 3 sentences, written in third person |
| Links and resources | Everything mentioned that has a link | Only links the user or guest gave |
| Credits and disclosure | Host, guest, producer, music, sponsor | One line each |
| Call to action | One next step | Subscribe, review, newsletter, or a question for listeners |

## Titles

- Lead with the idea, not the episode number: "Keeping Bees on a Hotel Roof with Daniel Okafor" beats "Ep. 48: Daniel Okafor".
- Use the words a listener would search: "rooftop beekeeping", "city honey".
- Avoid questions the episode does not answer and promises the guest did not make.

## Summaries

- Sentence 1: who and what, in plain words. Sentence 2: the most surprising or useful point.
- Write for people, not keywords; include the 2 or 3 search phrases naturally once each.
- No "In this episode we talk about..." filler; start with the substance.

## Key takeaways

Write each takeaway as a claim or instruction from the episode, not a topic:
- Weak: "Water on roofs."
- Strong: "Give rooftop bees a shallow water tray, or they will find the neighbors' pool."

## Chapter titles

- Describe what the listener gets in that part, in 2 to 6 words: "Why wind is the real enemy".
- Keep them parallel in style (all statements or all questions).
- Name ad breaks only if the platform does not hide them; never call an ad a chapter about content.

## Quotes

- Pick lines that stand alone: a clear claim, a lesson, a number, or a vivid image.
- Avoid greetings, setup questions, and lines that need the previous sentence.
- Removing fillers (um, uh, you know) is fine; mark the quote as lightly edited. Changing words is not.

## Accessibility and trust

- Link a full transcript when one exists; it helps deaf and hard-of-hearing listeners and search.
- Disclose sponsors and affiliate links clearly.
- Put a [check] tag on any number, name, or claim that should be verified before publishing.

# Chapters and platform rules

Rules change; when in doubt, check the platform's current help page. These are the stable basics.

## YouTube (video podcasts and audio uploads)

- Chapters come from timestamps in the description, one per line: `00:00 Intro`.
- The first timestamp must be 00:00.
- At least 3 timestamps, and each chapter at least 10 seconds long.
- Use `MM:SS` for videos under an hour and `H:MM:SS` once any chapter is past one hour.
- `chapterize.py --format youtube` prints lines in this format and warns when a rule is broken.

## Spotify

- Spotify reads chapter timestamps from the episode description in the same `MM:SS Title` style for episodes on its platform; follow the same rules as YouTube (start at 00:00, a few minutes apart).

## Apple Podcasts and most other apps

- Chapters are embedded in the audio file: ID3 CHAP frames in MP3 or a chapter track in M4A/AAC. Add them in the audio editor or a tagging tool before uploading.
- Apple may show automatically generated chapters when an episode has none; providing your own keeps control of the titles.

## Podcasting 2.0 (RSS)

- The `<podcast:chapters>` tag points to a JSON chapters file, supported by many modern apps and hosts:
```json
{
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "chapters": [
    { "startTime": 0, "title": "Intro" },
    { "startTime": 280, "title": "Keeping bees on a windy roof" }
  ]
}
```
- `startTime` is in seconds; `chapterize.py --format json` gives `start` in seconds for each chapter.

## Timestamps

- Transcript times often differ from the final file: intros, ads, and edits shift them. Use `--offset` for a fixed shift and recheck a few chapters in the audio.
- Without timestamps, `chapterize.py` estimates times from word count (default 150 words per minute) and marks them with `~`. Never publish estimated times without checking.
- Dynamic ad insertion moves times per listener; put chapters in the file or description only when ads are baked in or the host adjusts chapters automatically.

## How the script finds chapter starts

1. Headings (`# Title`, `Chapter 3: ...`, `Segment: ...`) always start a chapter.
2. Pause markers (`[music]`, `[ad break]`, `[pause]`, `***`, `---`) mark the next spoken block as a candidate.
3. Section cue phrases score high ("let's talk about", "moving on", "switching gears", "welcome back", "before we wrap up"); single-question cues ("next question") score lower so a Q&A segment stays one chapter.
4. Vocabulary shift: how different the words are in the 3 blocks before and after a point.
5. Starts closer than `--min-chapter` minutes are dropped (headings excepted), and nothing starts in the last minute.

## Quote and transcript ethics

- Keep quotes faithful; mark filler removal as an edit.
- Ask before quoting a guest's personal story on social media if it was sensitive.
- Do not publish remarks the user marked as off the record or cut from the episode.

# Keeping Bees on a Hotel Roof with Daniel Okafor

**Small Plot Radio** | Episode 48 | 26:02 | Guest: Daniel Okafor

Daniel Okafor keeps twelve beehives on a downtown hotel roof. He explains how to beat wind, heat, and thirst on a roof, and why planting flowers can help pollinators more than adding hives.

Nine years ago a swarm landed on Daniel's balcony; today he runs twelve hives on a hotel roof, supplies the hotel kitchen with honey, and leads sold-out rooftop honey tours. Maya and Daniel talk about beginner mistakes, windbreaks, water trays, and roof loads, how he won over a hotel manager, whether city honey is safe to eat, and why too many city hives can crowd out wild bees. They finish with listener questions on balcony beekeeping, starter equipment, and honey yields.

## Key takeaways

- Inspect hives every 7 to 10 days in spring, with a plan, and leave them alone in between.
- On a roof, wind is the main enemy: a 1.5 m slatted windbreak on the exposed sides makes the difference.
- Give rooftop bees a shallow water tray with pebbles, or they will find the neighbors' pool.
- Have the roof load checked first: a full hive can weigh 80 to 100 kg.
- Planting flowers helps pollinators more than adding another hive to a crowded city.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split a podcast transcript into rough chapter candidates and pull quote candidates.

Usage:
  python3 chapterize.py TRANSCRIPT [options]
  python3 chapterize.py - < transcript.txt          (read stdin)

Accepted input (detected automatically, can be mixed):
  - timestamp lines: "[00:12:30] Ana: text", "00:12:30 text", "(12:30) text", "12:30 - text"
  - WebVTT/SRT cue times: "00:01:02.000 --> 00:01:05.000" (the cue text follows)
  - headings: "# Intro", "## Part 2", "Chapter 3: Pricing", "SEGMENT: listener questions"
  - pause markers: [pause], [music], [break], [ad break], (long pause), ***, ---
  - plain paragraphs separated by blank lines (times are estimated from --wpm)

Options:
  --min-chapter MIN   shortest chapter in minutes (default 4)
  --max-chapters N    most chapters to return (default 12)
  --wpm N             speaking rate used to estimate times without timestamps (default 150)
  --offset SEC        seconds to add to every time, for an intro added in the edit (default 0)
  --quotes N          number of quote candidates (default 6)
  --format FMT        text (default), json, or youtube (chapter lines "00:00 Title")
  --duration HH:MM:SS total episode length, to check the last chapter and YouTube rules

Chapter boundaries come from headings first, then pause markers and cue phrases
("let's talk about", "moving on", "after the break"), then vocabulary shifts between
neighbouring blocks. Titles are keyword guesses: always rewrite them for the listener.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 input too short for chapters, 2 usage or read error.
Python 3 standard library only.
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter

TS_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*[\[(]?((?:\d{1,2}:)?\d{1,2}:\d{2})(?:[.,]\d+)?[\])]?\s*(?:[-\u2013\u2014|:]\s*)?(.*)$")
CUE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*((?:\d{1,2}:)?\d{1,2}:\d{2})[.,]\d{1,3}\s*-->\s*((?:\d{1,2}:)?\d{1,2}:\d{2})?")
LAST_CUE_END = [0]
HEADING = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:#{1,6}\s+(.+)|(?:chapter|part|segment|section|topic)\s*\d*\s*[:.\-\u2013]\s*(.+))\s*$", re.I)
PAUSE = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:\[(?:pause|long pause|music|break|ad break|ad|sponsor|interlude|silence)[^\]]*\]|"
                   r"\((?:pause|long pause|music|break|ad break|silence)[^)]*\)|\*{3,}|-{3,}|={3,})\s*$", re.I)
SPEAKER = re.compile(r"^([A-Z][\w.'-]*(?: [A-Z][\w.'-]*){0,2}):\s+(.*)$")
# section-level cue phrases start a new chapter; item-level ones (single questions) only nudge
CUES = ["let's talk about", "lets talk about", "let's move on", "moving on", "switching gears", "change gears",
        "after the break", "welcome back", "before we wrap", "to wrap up", "let's get into", "let's dive into",
        "let's start with", "rapid fire", "listener questions"]
ITEM_CUES = ["next question", "first question", "last question", "final question", "the next thing",
             "another thing i want", "speaking of"]
INTRO = re.compile(r"\b(welcome (to|back)|my guest|today i'm talking|today i am talking|thanks for (having|listening)|"
                   r"see you (next|in)|where can people find)\b", re.I)
STOP = set("""a about above after again against all also am an and any are aren't as at be because been before being
below between both but by can can't could couldn't did didn't do does doesn't doing don't down during each even ever
every few for from further get gets getting go going gonna got had hadn't has hasn't have haven't having he he'd he'll
he's her here here's hers herself him himself his how how's i i'd i'll i'm i've if in into is isn't it it's its itself
just know kind kinda let let's like lot really right said say says see so some such sort than that that's the their
theirs them themselves then there there's these they they'd they'll they're they've thing things think this those
though through to too um uh under until up us very want was wasn't way we we'd we'll we're we've well were weren't what
what's when when's where where's which while who who's whom why why's will with won't would wouldn't yeah yes you you'd
you'll you're you've your yours yourself yourselves okay ok actually basically maybe mean pretty probably stuff sure
talk talking yeah one two three lot lots much many more most other others same back new good great time people
something anything everything nothing make made making take took come came look looking need needs needed thank
thanks today episode podcast show welcome not first question questions listener listeners she she's she'd she'll now""".split())
QUOTE_WORDS = re.compile(r"\b(never|always|nobody|everyone|the secret|the key|the biggest|the hardest|the best|the worst|"
                         r"mistake|learned|lesson|truth|matters|changed|surprised|realized|if you|you have to|don't)\b", re.I)
FILLER = re.compile(r"\b(um+|uh+|you know|i mean|sort of|kind of|like,)\s*", re.I)


class UsageError(Exception):
    pass


def to_sec(ts):
    parts = [int(p) for p in ts.split(":")]
    while len(parts) < 3:
        parts.insert(0, 0)
    h, m, s = parts
    return h * 3600 + m * 60 + s


def fmt(sec, force_hours=False):
    sec = int(round(sec))
    h, rem = divmod(sec, 3600)
    m, s = divmod(rem, 60)
    return f"{h:d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d}" if h or force_hours else f"{m:02d}:{s:02d}"


def words(text):
    return re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'-]+", text)


def parse(text):
    """Return a list of units: dict(kind=text|heading|pause, text, time or None, speaker)."""
    units, pending_time = [], None
    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").lstrip("\ufeff").split("\n")
    para = []

    def flush():
        if para:
            joined = " ".join(p["text"] for p in para)
            units.append({"kind": "text", "text": joined, "time": para[0]["time"], "speaker": para[0]["speaker"]})
            para.clear()

    for raw in lines:
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.upper() == "WEBVTT" or line.isdigit():
            if not line:
                flush()
            continue
        m = CUE_LINE.match(line)
        if m:
            pending_time = to_sec(m.group(1))
            if m.group(2):
                LAST_CUE_END[0] = max(LAST_CUE_END[0], to_sec(m.group(2)))
            continue
        h = HEADING.match(line)
        if h:
            flush()
            units.append({"kind": "heading", "text": (h.group(1) or h.group(2)).strip(), "time": pending_time,
                          "speaker": None})
            continue
        if PAUSE.match(line):
            flush()
            units.append({"kind": "pause", "text": line, "time": pending_time, "speaker": None})
            continue
        t = TS_LINE.match(line)
        time = pending_time
        if t and t.group(2) is not None and (":" in t.group(1)):
            time, line = to_sec(t.group(1)), t.group(2).strip()
            flush()
            if not line:
                pending_time = time
                continue
            h = HEADING.match(line)
            if h:
                units.append({"kind": "heading", "text": (h.group(1) or h.group(2)).strip(), "time": time, "speaker": None})
                pending_time = None
                continue
            if PAUSE.match(line):
                units.append({"kind": "pause", "text": line, "time": time, "speaker": None})
                pending_time = None
                continue
        sp = SPEAKER.match(line)
        speaker = None
        if sp and len(sp.group(1)) <= 30:
            speaker, line = sp.group(1), sp.group(2)
            flush()
        if time is not None or pending_time is not None:
            flush()
        para.append({"text": line, "time": time, "speaker": speaker})
        pending_time = None
    flush()
    return units


def assign_times(units, wpm, offset):
    """Fill missing times by interpolating between known ones or from the word count."""
    known = [i for i, u in enumerate(units) if u["time"] is not None]
    clock = 0.0
    timed = bool(known)
    for i, u in enumerate(units):
        if u["time"] is not None:
            clock = float(u["time"])
            u["estimated"] = False
        else:
            u["time"] = clock
            u["estimated"] = True
        clock = u["time"] + len(words(u["text"])) / wpm * 60 if u["kind"] == "text" else u["time"]
    for u in units:
        u["time"] += offset
    return timed


EXTRA_STOP = set()


def keywords(text, n=4):
    ws = [w.lower().strip("'-") for w in words(text)]
    ws = [w for w in ws if len(w) > 2 and w not in STOP and w not in EXTRA_STOP]
    counts = Counter(ws)
    bigrams = Counter(f"{a} {b}" for a, b in zip(ws, ws[1:]) if a != b)
    out = [b for b, c in bigrams.most_common(3) if c >= 2]
    for w, _c in counts.most_common(12):
        if len(out) >= n:
            break
        if not any(w in b.split() for b in out):
            out.append(w)
    return out[:n]


def similarity(a, b):
    wa = {w.lower() for w in words(a) if w.lower() not in STOP and len(w) > 2}
    wb = {w.lower() for w in words(b) if w.lower() not in STOP and len(w) > 2}
    if not wa or not wb:
        return 0.0
    return len(wa & wb) / len(wa | wb)


def boundaries(units, min_gap, max_chapters, end_time):
    """Score each unit as a chapter start; return chosen indexes (always includes the first text unit)."""
    scores = {}
    for i, u in enumerate(units):
        if u["kind"] == "heading":
            scores[i] = 10.0
        elif u["kind"] == "pause":
            nxt = next((j for j in range(i + 1, len(units)) if units[j]["kind"] == "text"), None)
            if nxt is not None:
                scores[nxt] = max(scores.get(nxt, 0), 3.0)
        elif u["kind"] == "text":
            low = u["text"].lower()
            cue = 4.0 if any(c in low[:160] for c in CUES) else 1.5 if any(c in low[:160] for c in ITEM_CUES) else 0.0
            before = " ".join(x["text"] for x in units[max(0, i - 3):i] if x["kind"] == "text")
            after = " ".join(x["text"] for x in units[i:i + 3] if x["kind"] == "text")
            shift = 1.0 - similarity(before, after) if before and after else 0.0
            score = shift * 2.0 + cue
            if score > 1.6:
                scores[i] = max(scores.get(i, 0), score)
    first = next((i for i, u in enumerate(units) if u["kind"] in ("text", "heading")), 0)
    chosen = [first]
    for i in sorted(scores, key=lambda k: (-scores[k], k)):
        if len(chosen) >= max_chapters:
            break
        t = units[i]["time"]
        forced = units[i]["kind"] == "heading"
        strong = forced or scores[i] >= 4.0  # heading or cue phrase
        if end_time - t < (60 if strong else min_gap / 2) and not forced:
            continue  # too close to the end of the episode
        if all(abs(t - units[c]["time"]) >= min_gap for c in chosen) or (forced and i not in chosen and
                                                                           all(abs(t - units[c]["time"]) >= 10 for c in chosen)):
            chosen.append(i)
    return sorted(set(chosen)), scores


def sentences(text):
    return [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text) if s.strip()]


def quote_candidates(units, n):
    cands = []
    for u in units:
        if u["kind"] != "text":
            continue
        for s in sentences(u["text"]):
            clean = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", FILLER.sub("", s)).strip()
            wc = len(clean.split())
            if wc < 8 or wc > 40 or clean.endswith("?"):
                continue
            score = 0.0
            score += 2.0 if 12 <= wc <= 28 else 0.5
            score += 1.5 * len(QUOTE_WORDS.findall(clean))
            score += 1.0 if re.search(r"\b\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?\s*(%|percent|x|times|years|hours|days)\b", clean, re.I) else 0
            score += 0.5 if re.search(r"\b(I|we)\b", clean) else 0
            score -= 1.0 if FILLER.search(s) else 0
            score -= 3.0 if INTRO.search(clean) else 0
            cands.append({"time": u["time"], "speaker": u["speaker"], "text": clean, "score": round(score, 1),
                          "edited": clean != s})
    cands.sort(key=lambda c: (-c["score"], c["time"]))
    out, seen = [], set()
    for c in cands:
        key = c["text"][:40].lower()
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        out.append(c)
        if len(out) >= n:
            break
    return sorted(out, key=lambda c: c["time"])


def build(units, chosen, end_time):
    chapters = []
    for k, start in enumerate(chosen):
        stop = chosen[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(chosen) else len(units)
        seg = units[start:stop]
        text = " ".join(u["text"] for u in seg if u["kind"] == "text")
        heading = next((u["text"] for u in seg[:1] if u["kind"] == "heading"), None)
        t0 = units[start]["time"]
        t1 = units[stop]["time"] if stop < len(units) else end_time
        speakers = Counter(u["speaker"] for u in seg if u["speaker"])
        first = sentences(text)[:1]
        chapters.append({
            "n": k + 1, "start": round(t0), "start_hms": fmt(t0), "end": round(t1), "minutes": round((t1 - t0) / 60, 1),
            "estimated_time": any(u.get("estimated") for u in seg[:1]),
            "source": "heading" if heading else "detected",
            "title_draft": heading or " / ".join(keywords(text)).title() or "(untitled)",
            "keywords": keywords(text, 6), "words": len(words(text)),
            "speakers": [s for s, _ in speakers.most_common()],
            "opening_line": first[0][:160] if first else "",
        })
    return chapters


def youtube_lines(chapters):
    lines, problems = [], []
    if chapters and chapters[0]["start"] != 0:
        problems.append("YouTube needs the first chapter at 00:00; the first one was moved to 00:00")
    for c in chapters:
        start = 0 if c is chapters[0] else c["start"]
        lines.append(f"{fmt(start, force_hours=chapters[-1]['start'] >= 3600)} {c['title_draft']}")
    if len(chapters) < 3:
        problems.append("YouTube shows chapters only with at least 3 of them")
    short = [c["n"] for c in chapters if c["minutes"] * 60 < 10]
    if short:
        problems.append(f"chapters {short} are shorter than 10 seconds (YouTube minimum)")
    return lines, problems


def parse_args(argv):
    opts = {"file": None, "min_chapter": 4.0, "max_chapters": 12, "wpm": 150.0, "offset": 0.0, "quotes": 6,
            "format": "text", "duration": None}
    numeric = {"--min-chapter": ("min_chapter", float), "--max-chapters": ("max_chapters", int),
               "--wpm": ("wpm", float), "--offset": ("offset", float), "--quotes": ("quotes", int)}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in ("-h", "--help"):
            print(__doc__)
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in numeric or a in ("--format", "--duration"):
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                raise UsageError(f"{a} needs a value")
            v = argv[i + 1]
            if a == "--format":
                if v not in ("text", "json", "youtube"):
                    raise UsageError("--format must be text, json, or youtube")
                opts["format"] = v
            elif a == "--duration":
                if not re.fullmatch(r"(?:\d{1,2}:)?\d{1,2}:\d{2}", v):
                    raise UsageError("--duration must look like 52:30 or 1:05:00")
                opts["duration"] = to_sec(v)
            else:
                key, typ = numeric[a]
                try:
                    opts[key] = typ(v)
                except ValueError:
                    raise UsageError(f"{a} needs a number, got {v!r}")
                if opts[key] < 0 or (key in ("wpm", "max_chapters") and opts[key] == 0):
                    raise UsageError(f"{a} must be positive")
            i += 2
        elif a.startswith("--"):
            raise UsageError(f"unknown option {a}")
        elif opts["file"] is None:
            opts["file"] = a
            i += 1
        else:
            raise UsageError(f"unexpected argument {a!r}")
    if opts["file"] is None:
        raise UsageError("give a transcript file, or - for stdin")
    return opts


def main(argv):
    try:
        opts = parse_args(argv)
        if opts["file"] == "-":
            text = sys.stdin.read()
        else:
            with open(opts["file"], encoding="utf-8") as f:
                text = f.read()
    except UsageError as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
        print(f"error: cannot read {opts['file']}: {getattr(e, 'strerror', None) or e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    units = parse(text)
    total_words = sum(len(words(u["text"])) for u in units if u["kind"] == "text")
    if total_words < 50:
        print(f"error: only {total_words} words of transcript; need at least 50 to suggest chapters", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    timed = assign_times(units, opts["wpm"], opts["offset"])
    last = units[-1]
    end_time = last["time"] + (len(words(last["text"])) / opts["wpm"] * 60 if last["kind"] == "text" else 0)
    end_time = max(end_time, LAST_CUE_END[0] + opts["offset"] if LAST_CUE_END[0] else 0)
    if opts["duration"]:
        end_time = max(end_time, opts["duration"])
    EXTRA_STOP.update(w.lower() for u in units if u["speaker"] for w in u["speaker"].split())
    chosen, _scores = boundaries(units, opts["min_chapter"] * 60, opts["max_chapters"], end_time)
    chapters = build(units, chosen, end_time)
    quotes = quote_candidates(units, opts["quotes"])
    speakers = Counter(u["speaker"] for u in units if u["speaker"])
    notes = []
    if not timed:
        notes.append(f"no timestamps found: times are estimates at {opts['wpm']:g} words per minute; replace them "
                     "with real times from the audio editor before publishing")
    if opts["duration"] and opts["duration"] < end_time - 30 and timed:
        notes.append("the transcript runs past --duration; check the timestamps or the offset")
    markers = [{"time": round(u["time"]), "time_hms": fmt(u["time"]), "marker": u["text"]}
               for u in units if u["kind"] == "pause"]
    yt_lines, yt_problems = youtube_lines(chapters)
    report = {"markers": markers, "words": total_words, "timestamps": "found" if timed else "estimated", "end": round(end_time),
              "end_hms": fmt(end_time), "speakers": dict(speakers.most_common()), "chapters": chapters,
              "quotes": quotes, "youtube": yt_lines, "youtube_problems": yt_problems, "notes": notes}
    if opts["format"] == "json":
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 0
    if opts["format"] == "youtube":
        print("\n".join(yt_lines))
        for p in yt_problems + notes:
            print(f"# note: {p}")
        return 0
    spk = ", ".join(f"{s} ({c} turns)" for s, c in speakers.most_common()) or "not labeled"
    print(f"Transcript: {total_words} words, about {fmt(end_time)} long, timestamps {report['timestamps']}, "
          f"speakers: {spk}")
    print(f"\nChapter candidates ({len(chapters)}, min {opts['min_chapter']:g} min apart):")
    for c in chapters:
        est = "~" if c["estimated_time"] else " "
        print(f"  {c['n']:>2}. {est}{c['start_hms']:>8}  {c['minutes']:>5.1f} min  [{c['source']}] {c['title_draft']}")
        print(f"      keywords: {', '.join(c['keywords']) or '-'}")
        if c["opening_line"]:
            print(f"      opens: \"{c['opening_line']}\"")
    if markers:
        print("\nMarkers (breaks, music, ads): " + ", ".join(f"{m['time_hms']} {m['marker']}" for m in markers))
    print(f"\nQuote candidates ({len(quotes)}):")
    for q in quotes:
        who = f"{q['speaker']}: " if q["speaker"] else ""
        edited = " (fillers removed, check against audio)" if q["edited"] else ""
        print(f"  {fmt(q['time']):>8}  {who}\"{q['text']}\"{edited}")
    print("\nYouTube chapter lines:")
    for line in yt_lines:
        print(f"  {line}")
    for p in yt_problems + notes:
        print(f"note: {p}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
